title.zh: 卷501 列傳二百八十八 遗逸二
title.raw: 卷501 列傳二百八十八 遗逸二

sentences.zh: 李孔昭單者昌崔周田劉繼寧劉永錫彭之燦

translations.literal: Li Kongzhao, Shan Zhechang, Cui Zhoutian, Liu Jining, Liu Yongxi, Peng Zhican.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kongzhao, Shan Zhechang, Cui Zhoutian, Liu Jining, Liu Yongxi, and Peng Zhican.

sentences.zh: 徐枋戴易李天植理洪儲顧柔謙子祖禹冒襄陳貞慧

translations.literal: Xu Fang, Dai Yi, Li Tianzhi, Li Chang, Hong Chu, Gu Rouqian, his son Zuyu, Mao Xiang, Chen Zhenhui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fang, Dai Yi, Li Tianzhi, Li Chang, Hong Chu, Gu Rouqian and his son Zuyu, Mao Xiang, and Chen Zhenhui.

sentences.zh: 祁班孫兄理孫汪渢餘增遠周齊曾傅山子眉費密

translations.literal: Qi Bansun, his elder brother Lisun, Wang Ping, Yu Zengyuan, Zhou Qizeng, Fu Shan styled Zimei, Fei Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Bansun and his elder brother Qi Lisun, Wang Ping, Yu Zengyuan, Zhou Qizeng, Fu Shan (courtesy name Zimei), and Fei Mi.

sentences.zh: 王弘撰杜濬弟岕郭都賢陶汝鼐李世熊談遷

translations.literal: Wang Hongzhuan, Du Jun and his younger brother Kan, Guo Duxian, Tao Runai, Li Shixiong, Tan Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongzhuan, Du Jun and his younger brother Kan, Guo Duxian, Tao Runai, Li Shixiong, and Tan Qian.

sentences.zh: 李孔昭，字光四，薊州人。

translations.literal: Li Kongzhao, courtesy name Guangsi, was a native of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kongzhao, styled Guangsi, came from Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 性孤介，平居教授生徒，倡明理學。

translations.literal: His nature was solitary and upright; in ordinary life he instructed students and promoted Neo-Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: Solitary and uncompromising by nature, he spent his days teaching pupils and championing Neo-Confucian doctrine.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十五年進士，見世事日非，不赴廷對，以所給牌坊銀留助軍餉。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Chongzhen he passed the jinshi examination; seeing affairs daily worsen, he did not attend the palace audience and left the silver given for his memorial arch to aid military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the fifteenth year of Chongzhen. As the times grew worse day by day, he declined the palace audience and donated the stipend for his memorial arch to the army.

sentences.zh: 奉母隱盤山中，躬執樵採自給。

translations.literal: He supported his mother in seclusion on Mount Pan, personally cutting firewood to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He took his mother into seclusion on Mount Pan and supported them both by gathering firewood with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 母病，刲股療之。

translations.literal: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his thigh to treat her.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell ill, he cut flesh from his own thigh to make a medicine for her.

sentences.zh: 北都陷，素服哭於野者三載。

translations.literal: When the northern capital fell, he wore plain mourning dress and wept in the wilds for three years.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the northern capital, he wore undyed mourning and wept in the open country for three full years.

sentences.zh: 薊州城破，妻王殉難死，終身不再娶。

translations.literal: When Jizhou city was taken, his wife Wang died a martyr's death; he never married again in his lifetime.
translations.idiomatic: When Jizhou fell, his wife Wang died in the calamity. He never took another wife for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 形跡數易，人無識者。

translations.literal: He changed his whereabouts many times, and no one recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his haunts again and again, and no one knew who he was.

sentences.zh: 清初，詔求遺老，撫按交章薦，不出。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, an edict sought out old worthies of the former dynasty; governors and censors repeatedly recommended him in memorials, but he would not come forth.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qing, the throne called for surviving elders of the Ming. Regional officials memorialized him again and again, yet he refused to appear.

sentences.zh: 一日，當道遣吏持書幣往，遇負薪者，呼而問之，曰：「若識李進士耶？

translations.literal: One day the local authorities sent a clerk with letters and gifts; meeting a man carrying firewood, he called and asked him, saying, "Do you know Jinshi Li?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the authorities sent a clerk with letters and gifts. On the way he met a man carrying firewood, hailed him, and asked, "Do you know Jinshi Li?"

sentences.zh: 」負薪者詰得其故，以手遙指而去。

translations.literal: The firewood carrier questioned him and learned the reason, then pointed distantly with his hand and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The woodcutter pressed him until he learned why he had come, then pointed off into the distance and walked away.

sentences.zh: 吏至其室，虛矣。

translations.literal: The clerk reached his dwelling, but it was empty.
translations.idiomatic: When the clerk reached the house, no one was there.

sentences.zh: 鄰叟曰：「汝面失之。

translations.literal: A neighboring old man said, "You let him slip from under your nose."
translations.idiomatic: A neighbor said, "He was right in front of you and you missed him."

sentences.zh: 向所負薪者，李進士也！

translations.literal: The man who was just carrying firewood—that was Jinshi Li!
translations.idiomatic: The man carrying firewood you met—that was Jinshi Li!"

sentences.zh: 」後屢物色之，卒不得。

translations.literal: Afterward they searched for him many times but in the end could not find him.
translations.idiomatic: They searched for him again and again afterward, but never found him.

sentences.zh: 時有某孝廉，當上公車，輒止不行，曰：「吾出郭門一步，何面目見李光四乎？

translations.literal: At the time a certain xiucai, when it was time to go to the capital for the examination, always stopped and would not go, saying, "If I step one pace beyond the city gate, how could I face Li Guangsi?"
translations.idiomatic: There was a xiucai who, whenever the examination caravan was due to leave, would refuse to go, saying, "If I set foot outside the city gate, how could I bear to face Li Guangsi?"

sentences.zh: 會值邑中方興役，按戶簽夫，驅孔昭，孔昭曰：「吾力不能任，原出貲以代。

translations.literal: It happened that the district was undertaking public works and conscripted laborers household by household; they drove Kongzhao forward, and Kongzhao said, "My strength cannot bear the burden; I wish to pay money in lieu."
translations.idiomatic: Just then the county was launching a public works project and drafting laborers from every household. They pressed Kongzhao into service. He said, "I am not strong enough for this work. I will pay a substitute fee instead."

sentences.zh: 」吏持去。

translations.literal: The clerk took it and left.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk took the money and went away.

sentences.zh: 閱數日，大學士杜立德聞孔昭在邑，急往候之，吏聞，趨謝罪。

translations.literal: After several days Grand Secretary Du Lede heard that Kongzhao was in the district and hurried to call on him; when the clerk heard of this, he rushed to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Grand Secretary Du Lede learned that Kongzhao was in the county and hurried to visit him. When the clerk heard of it, he rushed over to beg forgiveness.

sentences.zh: 孔昭曰：「此間不知有李進士，若勿誤也。

translations.literal: Kongzhao said, "Around here no one has heard of Jinshi Li; you must be mistaken."
translations.idiomatic: Kongzhao said, "No one here has ever heard of a Jinshi Li. You must have the wrong man."

sentences.zh: 」由是跡愈密，或黃冠，或儒服，見者甚稀。

translations.literal: From this his tracks grew ever more hidden; sometimes in Daoist cap and robe, sometimes in scholar's dress—those who saw him were very few.
translations.idiomatic: After that he hid his tracks all the more closely, appearing sometimes in Daoist garb and sometimes in scholar's robes. Few people ever caught sight of him.

sentences.zh: 惟寶坻單者昌、崔周田、劉繼寧皆高士，與之友善，往來無虛歲。

translations.literal: Only Shan Zhechang, Cui Zhoutian, and Liu Jining of Baodi—all lofty scholars—were on friendly terms with him, and not a year passed without visits between them.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shan Zhechang, Cui Zhoutian, and Liu Jining of Baodi—men of the highest character—were his close friends, and they never let a year go by without meeting.

sentences.zh: 者昌，字蔚起。

translations.literal: Zhechang, courtesy name Weiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhechang, styled Weiqi.

sentences.zh: 才名埒孔昭。

translations.literal: His talent and reputation matched Kongzhao's.
translations.idiomatic: His literary fame rivaled Kongzhao's.

sentences.zh: 早餼於庠，入清不復應試。

translations.literal: He had early received a stipend from the academy; after the Qing entry he never again sat for the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He had long held a government stipend as a student of the academy. After the Qing conquest he never took the examinations again.

sentences.zh: 杜立德招之，不能致，獨與孔昭徜徉田野間，悲歌慨憤，有所作，輒焚之，不以示人。

translations.literal: Du Lede invited him but could not bring him; he alone with Kongzhao wandered in fields and meadows, singing sadly with indignant passion; whatever he wrote he at once burned and did not show to others.
translations.idiomatic: Du Lede tried to summon him but could not. He wandered the countryside with Kongzhao alone, singing laments full of grief and rage. Whatever he wrote he burned at once and never showed anyone.

sentences.zh: 竟以憂死。

translations.literal: In the end he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: He died of grief in the end.

sentences.zh: 周田，字錫齡。

translations.literal: Zhoutian, courtesy name Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhoutian, styled Xiling.

sentences.zh: 順治中，充歲貢，不與試。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi reign he qualified as annual tribute student but did not take the examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shunzhi reign he was nominated as a tribute student but declined to sit for the examination.

sentences.zh: 建一樓，貯古本書及金石刻萬卷，日吟嘯其中。

translations.literal: He built a tower, stored therein ten thousand scrolls of ancient books and stone and bronze inscriptions, and daily chanted and whistled within it.
translations.idiomatic: He built a tower and filled it with ten thousand volumes of rare books and rubbings of stone and bronze inscriptions, spending his days chanting and singing there.

sentences.zh: 嘗過盤山，與孔昭坐林石間相笑語。

translations.literal: He once passed Mount Pan and sat with Kongzhao among forest rocks, laughing and talking together.
translations.idiomatic: He once visited Mount Pan and sat with Kongzhao among the trees and boulders, laughing and talking together.

sentences.zh: 孔昭亦時下榻於其家，周田命其子執弟子禮，且迎孔昭母，事之如所生。

translations.literal: Kongzhao also sometimes lodged at his home; Zhoutian ordered his son to perform the disciple's rites, and moreover welcomed Kongzhao's mother, serving her as if she were his own parent.
translations.idiomatic: Kongzhao sometimes stayed at his home as well. Zhoutian had his son observe the rites due a teacher, and he welcomed Kongzhao's mother and cared for her as if she were his own.

sentences.zh: 繼寧，字兌菴。

translations.literal: Jining, courtesy name Duian.
translations.idiomatic: Jining, styled Duian.

sentences.zh: 少負義氣，有古俠士風。

translations.literal: In youth he bore righteous spirit and had the air of an ancient knight-errant.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was known for his sense of justice and carried himself like the chivalrous men of old.

sentences.zh: 嘗出重金贖難女二，為之擇配。

translations.literal: He once paid a heavy sum to redeem two women in distress and found husbands for them.
translations.idiomatic: He once paid a large sum to ransom two women in distress and found suitable husbands for them.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，煮粥食餓者。

translations.literal: In years of famine he cooked gruel to feed the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years he cooked porridge to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 視周田如手足，有緩急恆資之，周田亦弗謝也。

translations.literal: He regarded Zhoutian as brother; whenever there was urgency he always supplied him, and Zhoutian also did not thank him.
translations.idiomatic: He treated Zhoutian like a brother, always helping him in times of need, and Zhoutian never made a fuss of thanking him.

sentences.zh: 晚年為子擇師遊盤山，跡孔昭，得之。

translations.literal: In his later years, to choose a teacher for his son he traveled Mount Pan tracking Kongzhao and found him.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he went to Mount Pan in search of a teacher for his son, tracked down Kongzhao, and found him.

sentences.zh: 邀至其家，令其三子從受業。

translations.literal: He invited him to his home and had his three sons follow and receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He invited Kongzhao to his home and had his three sons study under him.

sentences.zh: 暇則與周田聚宴歌呼以為樂，然每一念母，雖深夜必馳歸，弗能禁也。

translations.literal: In leisure he would gather with Zhoutian for feasts, singing and calling out for joy; yet whenever he thought of his mother, even in deep night he must gallop home and could not restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: In his free time he feasted and sang with Zhoutian for pleasure. Yet whenever he thought of his mother, he would ride home at once, even in the dead of night, and could not stop himself.

sentences.zh: 晚好陶詩，因又自號潛翁。

translations.literal: In later life he loved Tao Yuanming's poetry and therefore also styled himself Hermit Weng.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he came to love Tao Yuanming's poetry and took the sobriquet Hermit Weng.

sentences.zh: 一日，為門人講孟子盡心章，曰：「此傳心法也！

translations.literal: One day, lecturing his disciples on Mencius's chapter "Fully Devoting the Mind," he said, "This transmits the mind-method!"
translations.idiomatic: One day, while lecturing his disciples on Mencius's "Fully Devoting the Mind," he said, "This is the transmission of the mind-method!"

sentences.zh: 」言訖而卒。

translations.literal: When the words were finished he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died as soon as he had spoken.

sentences.zh: 其弟子私諡曰安節先生。

translations.literal: His disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master Anjie.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples privately honored him with the posthumous title Master Anjie.

sentences.zh: 劉永錫，字欽爾，號賸菴，魏縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Yongxi, courtesy name Qiner, sobriquet Shengan, was a native of Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yongxi, styled Qiner, known as Shengan, came from Wei County.

sentences.zh: 崇禎乙亥舉人，官長洲教諭。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen's yihai year he passed the provincial examination and served as instructor at Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the yihai year of Chongzhen and served as director of studies at Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 南都敗，率妻栗隱居相城，大吏造其室，欲強之出，永錫袒裼疾視，曰：「我中原男子，年二十，渡漳河，登大伾，躍馬鳴鞘，兩河豪傑，誰不知我者！

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital fell, he led his wife Li into seclusion at Xiangcheng; a high official came to his dwelling wishing to force him out; Yongxi bared his torso and glared fiercely, saying, "I am a man of the Central Plains; at twenty I crossed the Zhang River, climbed Mount Daqi, leaped on horseback with clashing scabbard—the heroes of the two rivers, who does not know me!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Capital fell, he took his wife Li into hiding at Xiangcheng. A senior official came to his home and tried to force him into service. Yongxi stripped to the waist and glared at him. "I am a man of the heartland," he said. "At twenty I crossed the Zhang River and climbed Mount Daqi, riding hard with my scabbard clashing at my side. Who among the heroes of the two rivers does not know my name?"

sentences.zh: 欲見辱耶？

translations.literal: Do you wish to insult me?
translations.idiomatic: Do you mean to dishonor me?"

sentences.zh: 」取壁上劍自刎。

translations.literal: He took the sword from the wall and tried to cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the sword from the wall and tried to cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 門下士抱持之，得解，謂其妻曰：「彼再至，我與若立決矣！

translations.literal: His disciples held him and he was released; he told his wife, "If they come again, you and I will settle it on the spot at once!"
translations.idiomatic: His disciples seized him and stopped him. He told his wife, "If they come again, you and I will settle the matter on the spot at once!"

sentences.zh: 」皆裂尺帛握之。

translations.literal: They all tore a foot of silk and gripped it.
translations.idiomatic: They each tore off a strip of silk and kept it in their hands.

sentences.zh: 尋移居陽城湖濱，與妻及子臨、女貞織蓆以食。

translations.literal: Soon they moved to dwell by Yangcheng Lake; with his wife and son Lin and daughter Zhen he wove mats for food.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they moved to the shore of Yangcheng Lake. He, his wife, his son Lin, and his daughter Zhen wove mats to live on.

sentences.zh: 市中見永錫攜席至，皆呼席先生。

translations.literal: When the market saw Yongxi carrying mats, all called him Master Mat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever people in the market saw Yongxi bringing in his mats, they called him Master Mat.

sentences.zh: 食不繼，時不舉火，有遺之粟者，非其人不受，益困憊。

translations.literal: Food did not continue; sometimes they did not light the fire; when someone sent grain, if it was not from the right person he would not accept it, and grew ever more exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Food ran out and they often went without cooking. When grain was sent to them, he refused it unless it came from someone he respected, and their hardship grew worse.

sentences.zh: 其女已許字，未嫁，亂後恐遭辱，絕粒死。

translations.literal: His daughter had been betrothed but not yet married; after the turmoil, fearing dishonor, she starved herself to death.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter had been betrothed but not yet married. After the chaos she feared being violated and starved herself to death.

sentences.zh: 其妻哭之成疾，亦死。

translations.literal: His wife wept until she fell ill and also died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife wept herself into illness over the girl and died as well.

sentences.zh: 其僮僕遇水災乏食，相繼餓死，或散走。

translations.literal: His servants and bondsmen, meeting flood and lack of food, died of hunger one after another, or scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: His servants, caught in the floods and short of food, starved to death one after another or fled.

sentences.zh: 有老奴從魏縣來，勸之歸，曰：「室廬故在也！

translations.literal: An old bondsman came from Wei County and urged him to return, saying, "The house and buildings are still there as before!"
translations.idiomatic: An old servant came from Wei County and urged him to go home. "Your house is still standing," he said.

sentences.zh: 」永錫曰：「我非不欲歸，然昔奉君命來，義不可離此一步。

translations.literal: Yongxi said, "It is not that I do not wish to return, but formerly I came on the lord's command; by righteousness I cannot leave this place one step."
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi said, "It is not that I do not want to go back. I came here on my lord's commission. By duty I cannot leave this place a single step."

sentences.zh: 」命其子與婦攜老奴還裡，曰：「祖宗丘墓責在汝！

translations.literal: He ordered his son and daughter-in-law to take the old bondsman back home, saying, "The charge of the ancestral graves rests on you!"
translations.idiomatic: He told his son and daughter-in-law to take the old servant home. "The duty to our ancestors' graves is yours," he said.

sentences.zh: 」麾之去。

translations.literal: He waved them away.
translations.idiomatic: He waved them off.

sentences.zh: 時歲荒，得食愈艱，每雜糠籺作飯。

translations.literal: At the time the year was famine-stricken and obtaining food grew harder; each time he mixed chaff and coarse grain to make rice.
translations.idiomatic: Famine made food ever harder to come by. He mixed chaff and bran into whatever he could cook.

sentences.zh: 臨既歸，思父不置，假貸得百金馳獻，中途馬驚，墮地死。

translations.literal: After Lin had returned home, unable to stop thinking of his father, he borrowed a hundred taels of gold and rushed to present them; midway the horse was startled, he fell to the ground and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Lin returned home he could not stop thinking of his father. He borrowed a hundred taels of gold and raced to bring them to him. On the way his horse bolted, he was thrown to the ground, and died.

sentences.zh: 永錫容貌甚偉，至是，毀形骨立，既自悼無家，買一破船往來江湖間。

translations.literal: Yongxi's appearance had been very imposing; by now his form was ruined and his bones stood out; grieving that he had no home, he bought a broken boat and went back and forth on rivers and lakes.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi had once been a striking figure. Now he was wasted to the bone. Mourning that he had no home left, he bought a broken boat and drifted on the rivers and lakes.

sentences.zh: 嘗泛舟中流，鼓枻而歌曰：「溯彼中流兮，採其荇矣。

translations.literal: Once he poled his boat midstream, beat the oar, and sang: "Against that midstream flow—gathering its water-chestnuts."
translations.idiomatic: Once he poled his boat into midstream, beat the oars, and sang: "Against the midstream current—gathering water-chestnuts."

sentences.zh: 呼君與父兮，莫之應矣。

translations.literal: "Calling lord and father—none answers."
translations.idiomatic: "I call to my lord and my father—no one answers."

sentences.zh: 身為餓夫兮，天所命矣。

translations.literal: "Body a starving man—heaven's decree."
translations.idiomatic: "My body is a starving man's—heaven has willed it."

sentences.zh: 中心殷殷兮，涕斯迸矣。

translations.literal: "Heart within deeply grieved—tears burst forth."
translations.idiomatic: "Grief wells in my heart—tears burst forth."

sentences.zh: 」又歌曰；

translations.literal: He sang again:
translations.idiomatic: He sang again:

sentences.zh: 「白日墮兮野荒荒，逐鳧鴈兮侶牛羊，壯士何心兮歸故鄉。

translations.literal: "White sun falls—the wilds desolate; chasing wild ducks and geese—keeping company with cattle and sheep; what heart has the stalwart man to return to his old home?"
translations.idiomatic: "The white sun sinks over empty wilds; I chase wild ducks and geese and keep company with cattle and sheep. What heart has a man like me to think of going home?"

sentences.zh: 」歌聲悲烈，聞者哀之。

translations.literal: His singing voice was mournful and fierce; those who heard were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: His voice was fierce with grief, and all who heard him were moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 尚書錢謙益念其窮，招之往，永錫曰：「尚書為黨魁，受主眷，枚卜時天子期以伊、傅，彼豈忘之邪？

translations.literal: Minister Qian Qianyi, pitying his poverty, invited him to come; Yongxi said, "The Minister was leader of the faction, received the lord's favor; when the divining rods were cast the Son of Heaven looked to him as Yi Yin and Fu Yue—how could he forget that?"
translations.idiomatic: Minister Qian Qianyi, moved by his poverty, invited him to come. Yongxi said, "The Minister was head of the party and enjoyed the emperor's trust. When the court sought a chief minister, the Son of Heaven looked to him as another Yi Yin or Fu Yue. Has he truly forgotten that?"

sentences.zh: 」卻不往，卒窮餓至不能起。

translations.literal: He declined and did not go; in the end he was so poor and hungry he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He refused and did not go. In the end he starved until he could no longer rise.

sentences.zh: 一夕，大呼「烈皇帝」者三，遂卒，時順治十一年秋也。

translations.literal: One night he cried out "Emperor Lie" three times, then died; it was autumn of the eleventh year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: One night he cried out "Emperor Lie" three times and died. It was autumn in the eleventh year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 弟子長洲徐晟、陳三島，友人常熟陸泓，經紀其喪，葬之於虎丘山塘，以妻、女祔之。

translations.literal: His disciples Xu Sheng of Changzhou and Chen Sandao, and his friend Lu Hong of Changshu, arranged his funeral and buried him at Shantang on Tiger Hill, with his wife and daughter joined in the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples Xu Sheng of Changzhou and Chen Sandao, and his friend Lu Hong of Changshu, arranged his funeral and buried him at Shantang on Tiger Hill, with his wife and daughter buried beside him.

sentences.zh: 彭之燦，字了凡，蠡縣諸生。

translations.literal: Peng Zhican, courtesy name Liaofan, was a licentiate of Li County.
translations.idiomatic: Peng Zhican, styled Liaofan, was a licentiate of Li County.

sentences.zh: 甲申後攜妻寓饒陽作村塾師。

translations.literal: After jiashen he took his wife to lodge at Raoyang and served as a village schoolteacher.
translations.idiomatic: After the jiashen year he took his wife to Raoyang and taught in a village school.

sentences.zh: 未幾，妻、子相繼死，至蘇門，與孫奇逢遊。

translations.literal: Before long his wife and son died in succession; he went to Sumen and associated with Sun Qifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Before long his wife and son died one after another. He went to Sumen and became a companion of Sun Qifeng.

sentences.zh: 然性不諧俗，愛靜坐。

translations.literal: Yet his nature did not harmonize with the vulgar; he loved quiet sitting.
translations.idiomatic: His nature, however, could not abide the world. He loved solitary meditation.

sentences.zh: 有人延於家，以市囂，輒避去。

translations.literal: When someone invited him to stay in their home, because of the market clamor he would at once avoid and leave.
translations.idiomatic: If someone invited him to stay in their home, the noise of the marketplace drove him away at once.

sentences.zh: 嘗渡河南游，韓鼎業為館之僧舍，年餘，又棄去。

translations.literal: He once crossed south of the river to travel; Han Dingye lodged him in a monastic cell for more than a year, then he abandoned it and left again.
translations.idiomatic: He once traveled south of the Yellow River. Han Dingye put him up in a monastery for more than a year, but he left again.

sentences.zh: 獨擔瓢笠圖書，遍遊嵩、少、王屋諸名勝。

translations.literal: Alone he shouldered gourd, bamboo hat, books, and maps, traveling everywhere to Mount Song, Mount Shao, Mount Wangwu, and other famous sites.
translations.idiomatic: Alone he carried his gourd, hat, books, and maps, wandering to Mount Song, Mount Shao, Mount Wangwu, and other famous peaks.

sentences.zh: 在九山絕粒數日，奇逢挽之夏峰，勸歸老先人墓旁。

translations.literal: On Jiushan he abstained from grain for several days; Qifeng drew him to Xiafeng and urged him to return and grow old beside his forefathers' tombs.
translations.idiomatic: On Jiushan he fasted for several days. Qifeng brought him to Xiafeng and urged him to go home and spend his old age by his ancestors' graves.

sentences.zh: 之燦曰：「某出門時，已誓告先壟不再返，不能蹈東海、入西山而死，即溝壑道路，無恨也！

translations.literal: Zhican said, "When I left home I had already sworn before the ancestral mound that I would not return; if I cannot tread the Eastern Sea or enter the Western Hills to die, then even in ditch or roadside, I have no regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhican said, "When I left home I swore at my ancestors' graves that I would never return. If I cannot die by drowning in the eastern sea or perishing on the western hills, I have no regret even if I die in a ditch by the roadside!"

sentences.zh: 」順治十五年六月，竟死嘯台東北石柱下。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he finally died beneath the stone pillar northeast of Xiaotai.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Shunzhi he died at last beneath the stone pillar northeast of Xiaotai.

sentences.zh: 奇逢為鐫石記其事，立墓上，曰「餓夫之墓」。

translations.literal: Qifeng had stone carved to record the affair and set it on the tomb, reading "Tomb of the Starving Man."
translations.idiomatic: Qifeng had an inscription cut in stone recording what had happened and set it on the grave: "Tomb of the Starving Man."

sentences.zh: 之燦與容城張果中、西華理鬯和，並稱「蘇門三賢。

translations.literal: Zhican together with Zhang Guozhong of Rongcheng and Li Changhe of Xihua were together called "the Three Worthies of Sumen."
translations.idiomatic: Zhican, together with Zhang Guozhong of Rongcheng and Li Changhe of Xihua, were known as the Three Worthies of Sumen.

sentences.zh: 徐枋，字昭法，長洲人。

translations.literal: Xu Fang, courtesy name Zhaofa, was a native of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fang, styled Zhaofa, came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 父汧，明少詹事，殉國難，事具明史。

translations.literal: His father Qian was Junior Mentor of the Ming and died a martyr in the national calamity; his affairs are fully recorded in the History of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qian was Junior Mentor under the Ming and died for the dynasty. His story is told in full in the History of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 枋，崇禎壬午舉人。

translations.literal: Fang passed the provincial examination in Chongzhen's renwu year.
translations.idiomatic: Fang passed the provincial examination in the renwu year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 汧殉國時，枋欲從死，汧曰；

translations.literal: When Qian died for the state, Fang wished to follow him in death; Qian said:
translations.idiomatic: When Qian died for the dynasty, Fang wanted to die with him. Qian said:

sentences.zh: 「吾不可以不死，若長為農夫以沒世可也！

translations.literal: "I cannot but die; you may long be a farmer and end your days—that is acceptable!"
translations.idiomatic: "I cannot but die. You may live out your days as a farmer—that is enough!"

sentences.zh: 」自是遁跡山中，布衣草履，終身不入城市。

translations.literal: From this he hid his tracks in the mountains, wore cloth robes and straw sandals, and throughout his life never entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he hid in the mountains in plain cloth and straw sandals, and never entered a city for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 及遊靈巖山，愛其曠遠，卜澗上居之，老焉。

translations.literal: When he visited Mount Lingyan he loved its open distance, chose a dwelling above the stream, and grew old there.
translations.idiomatic: When he visited Mount Lingyan he loved its open vistas and settled above a stream, where he lived out his old age.

sentences.zh: 枋與宣城沈壽民、嘉興巢鳴盛，稱「海內三遺民」。

translations.literal: Fang, together with Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng and Chao Mingsheng of Jiaxing, were called the "Three Remnant Subjects Within the Seas."
translations.idiomatic: Fang, Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng, and Chao Mingsheng of Jiaxing were known throughout the realm as the "Three Loyalist Survivors."

sentences.zh: 枋書法孫過庭，畫宗巨然，間法倪、黃，自署秦餘山人。

translations.literal: Fang's calligraphy followed Sun Guoting; his painting took Juran as patriarch, occasionally also the methods of Ni and Huang; he signed himself Mountain Man of Qin Remnants.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy followed Sun Guoting; his painting looked to Juran, with occasional debts to Ni Zan and Huang Gongwang, and he styled himself the Qin Remnant Mountain Man.

sentences.zh: 嘗寄靈芝一貞於王士禎，士禎與金孝章畫梅、王玠草書作齋中三詠以記之。

translations.literal: Once he sent Wang Shizhen a single stalk of lingzhi; Shizhen, together with Jin Xiaozhang's plum painting and Wang Jie's cursive script, composed three verses for his studio to record it.
translations.idiomatic: He once sent Wang Shizhen a single lingzhi fungus; Shizhen commemorated the gift with three poems for his study, pairing them with Jin Xiaozhang's painting of plum blossoms and Wang Jie's cursive calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 然性峻介，鍵戶勿與人接。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was stern and unyielding; he bolted his door and would have no dealings with others.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was stern and unbending by nature, kept his door barred, and refused all contact with the outside world.

sentences.zh: 睢州湯斌巡撫江南，屏騶從，往訪之，枋避不見。

translations.literal: Tang Bin of Suizhou, as governor-general of Jiangnan, dismissed his mounted escort and went to visit him; Fang avoided him and would not appear.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Bin of Suizhou became governor-general of Jiangnan, he left his mounted escort behind and came to call on Fang, who hid and refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 斌登其堂，堅坐移晷，為誦白駒之詩，週覽太息而去。

translations.literal: Bin entered his hall, sat steadfastly for a watch of the day, recited for him the poem "White Colt," looked all around sighing, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Bin entered his hall anyway, sat there unmoving for hours, recited the Book of Songs poem "White Colt" to the empty room, gazed about with a long sigh, and left.

sentences.zh: 川湖總督蔡毓榮自荊州致書求其畫，枋答書而返幣，竟不為作。

translations.literal: Cai Yurong, Governor-General of Chuanhu, wrote from Jingzhou asking for his painting; Fang wrote back and returned the gift, and in the end would not paint for him.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yurong, governor-general of Chuan and Hu, wrote from Jingzhou requesting a painting; Fang replied by letter, sent the gift back, and never produced the work.

sentences.zh: 曰：「明府是殷荊州，吾薄顧長康不為耳。

translations.literal: He said: "Your Excellency is Yin Jingzhou; I merely think lightly of Gu Changkang's refusal—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote back: "Your Excellency is another Yin Zhongkan—but I am no more willing to paint than Gu Kaizhi was for his officials.

sentences.zh: 」所往來惟沈壽民與萊陽姜垓、同里楊無咎、門人吳江潘耒及南嶽僧洪儲而已。

translations.literal: " Those with whom he associated were only Shen Shoumin, Jiang Kai of Laiyang, Yang Wujiu of his native place, his disciple Pan Lei of Wujiang, and the Mount Heng monk Hong Chu—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: Those were the only people he kept company with: Shen Shoumin, Jiang Kai of Laiyang, his fellow townsman Yang Wujiu, his disciple Pan Lei of Wujiang, and the monk Hong Chu of Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 家貧絕糧，耐飢寒，不受人一絲一粟。

translations.literal: His household was poor and grainless; he endured hunger and cold and would not accept from others a single thread or grain of rice.
translations.idiomatic: His family was destitute and often without grain; he bore hunger and cold and would not take a thread or a grain from anyone.

sentences.zh: 洪儲時其急而周之，枋曰：「此世外清淨食也。

translations.literal: Hong Chu at times when he was in straits would relieve him; Fang said: "This is pure food from beyond the world."
translations.idiomatic: When Fang was in dire need, Hong Chu would help him along; Fang said, "This is the pure sustenance of one outside the world."

sentences.zh: 」無不受。

translations.literal: " He never failed to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: "—and he never refused a single gift from him.

sentences.zh: 豢一驢，通人意。

translations.literal: He raised a donkey that understood human intent.
translations.idiomatic: He kept a donkey that seemed to understand what he wanted.

sentences.zh: 日用間有所需，則以所作書畫卷置簏於驢背，驅之。

translations.literal: When in daily life he needed something, he would place scrolls of his calligraphy and painting in a basket on the donkey's back and drive it off.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he needed something for daily life, he would load a basket on the donkey's back with scrolls of his own painting and calligraphy and send it on its way.

sentences.zh: 驢獨行，及城闉而止，不闌入一步。

translations.literal: The donkey went alone, and when it reached the suburb of the wall it stopped, not crossing in a single step.
translations.idiomatic: The donkey went by itself and halted at the city gate, never stepping a foot inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 見者爭趣之，曰：「高士驢至矣！

translations.literal: Those who saw it would rush to it, saying: "The lofty gentleman's donkey has come!"
translations.idiomatic: People who saw it would hurry over, crying, "The recluse's donkey is here!"

sentences.zh: 」亟取卷，以日用所需物，如其指，備而納諸簏，驢即負以返，以為常。

translations.literal: " They would hasten to take the scrolls, supply daily necessities as indicated, prepare them and put them in the basket, and the donkey would bear them back at once—this became the routine.
translations.idiomatic: They would take the scrolls at once, fill the basket with whatever daily goods were wanted, and send the donkey home loaded—a routine that never varied.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 時商丘宋犖撫吳，枋預戒曰；

translations.literal: At the time Song Luo of Shangqiu was governing Wu; Fang gave advance warning, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Song Luo of Shangqiu was governor of Wu, Fang left instructions in advance:

sentences.zh: 「宋中丞甚知我，若我死，勿受其賻也。

translations.literal: "Vice Minister Song knows me well; if I die, do not accept funeral gifts from him."
translations.idiomatic: "Commissioner Song knows me well—if I die, do not accept any funeral gift from him."

sentences.zh: 」犖果使人贈棺槥貲如枋命，終不受。

translations.literal: " Luo indeed sent someone to present coffin funds as Fang had foreseen, but in the end they were not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Song did send money for a coffin, just as Fang had foreseen, but the family refused it to the end.

sentences.zh: 卒，以貧不能葬。

translations.literal: When he died, they were too poor to bury him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his family was too poor to bury him.

sentences.zh: 一日，有高士從武林來吊，請任窀穹，其人亦貧，而特工篆、隸，乃賃居郡中。

translations.literal: One day a lofty gentleman came from Wulin to mourn, offered to take charge of the burial; that man was also poor, but specialized in seal and clerical script, and so rented lodging in the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: One day a recluse came from Wulin to pay his respects and offered to handle the burial; he too was poor, but excelled at seal and clerical script, and took a rented room in the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 鬻字以庀葬具，紙得百錢。

translations.literal: He sold characters to prepare funeral goods; each sheet brought a hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: He sold his calligraphy to pay for the funeral, charging a hundred cash per sheet.

sentences.zh: 積二年，乃克葬枋於青芝山下，而以羨歸其家。

translations.literal: Accumulating for two years, he was finally able to bury Fang below Mount Qingzhi, and returned the surplus to his family.
translations.idiomatic: After two years of saving he was able to bury Fang at the foot of Mount Qingzhi and gave the leftover money to the family.

sentences.zh: 語之曰：「吾欲稱貸富家，懼先生吐之，故勞吾腕，知先生所心許也。

translations.literal: He said to them: "I wished to borrow from a rich house, fearing the Master would spit at it; therefore I have wearied my wrist—you know this is what the Master would approve in his heart."
translations.idiomatic: He told them, "I thought of borrowing from a wealthy family, but feared the Master would have been disgusted—so I wore out my wrist instead; you know he would have approved."

sentences.zh: 」葬畢即去，不言名氏。

translations.literal: " When the burial was complete he left at once, not speaking his name.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the burial was done he left without giving his name.

sentences.zh: 或有識之者，曰：「此山陰戴易也！

translations.literal: Someone who recognized him said: "This is Dai Yi of Shanyin!"
translations.idiomatic: Someone who knew him exclaimed, "That was Dai Yi of Shanyin!"

sentences.zh: 易，字南枝。

translations.literal: Yi, courtesy name Nazhi.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Yi, styled Nazhi.

sentences.zh: 少從劉宗周學，遊吳門，年七十餘矣。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Liu Zongzhou; he traveled to Wu gate and was already over seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he had studied under Liu Zongzhou; he had come to the Suzhou region and was already past seventy.

sentences.zh: 有六子，不受其養，獨攜一子及殘書百卷自隨。

translations.literal: He had six sons but would not accept their support, taking only one son and a hundred volumes of surviving books with him.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons but would not live on their support, keeping only one son and a hundred battered volumes of books with him.

sentences.zh: 其售字也，銖積寸累，不妄費一錢。

translations.literal: In selling characters he amassed bit by bit, not spending a single coin recklessly.
translations.idiomatic: The money he earned from selling calligraphy he hoarded penny by penny and never spent a single cash carelessly.

sentences.zh: 一蒼頭飢不能忍，輒逃去。

translations.literal: One grey-haired servant, unable to endure hunger, would flee at times.
translations.idiomatic: One old servant, unable to bear the hunger, would run away.

sentences.zh: 己寄食僧舍中，語及枋，必流涕。

translations.literal: He had lodged in a monks' quarters; when the conversation touched Fang, he would always weep.
translations.idiomatic: He was living on charity in a monastery, and whenever Fang's name came up he would burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 嘗浮七里瀨，登嚴子陵釣台，賦詩，且歌且泣。

translations.literal: Once he floated on the Qili Shoals, climbed Yan Ziling's Fishing Terrace, composed a poem, and sang and wept as he went.
translations.idiomatic: He once sailed the Qili Rapids, climbed Yan Ziling's Fishing Terrace, wrote a poem there, and sang and wept by turns.

sentences.zh: 或竟日不得食，採野蕨充膳。

translations.literal: At times he could get no food all day and would gather wild bracken to fill his meal.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes he went a whole day without food and would gather wild ferns to eat.

sentences.zh: 操瓢量水，坐長松古石間飲之。

translations.literal: He took a gourd to measure water and sat among ancient pines and rocks drinking it.
translations.idiomatic: He would dip a gourd for water and drink it seated among ancient pines and boulders.

sentences.zh: 李天植，字因仲，平湖人。

translations.literal: Li Tianzhi, courtesy name Yinzhong, was a native of Pinghu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tianzhi, styled Yinzhong, came from Pinghu.

sentences.zh: 崇禎癸酉舉人。

translations.literal: In Chongzhen's guiyou year he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the guiyou year of Chongzhen.

sentences.zh: 改名確，字潛夫。

translations.literal: He changed his name to Que and styled himself Qianfu.
translations.idiomatic: He later changed his name to Que and took the style Qianfu.

sentences.zh: 甲申後，餘田四十畝、宅一區，乃並家具分與所後子震及女，而與妻別隱陳山，絕跡不入城市，訓山中童子自給。

translations.literal: After jiashen, his remaining forty mu of fields and one residence, together with household goods he divided among his son Zhen by a later wife and his daughter; he and his wife separately hid on Mount Chen, cutting off tracks and not entering the city, training mountain lads for self-support.
translations.idiomatic: After 1644 he gave away his remaining forty mu of land, his house, and all the furnishings to his son Zhen by a later marriage and to his daughter; he and his wife withdrew separately to Mount Chen, never set foot in town again, and taught village boys for their keep.

sentences.zh: 居十年，以僧開堂，始避喧，返蜃園，賣文自食；

translations.literal: After ten years' residence, because a monk opened a lecture hall, he first fled the clamor and returned to Mirage Garden, supporting himself by selling writings;
translations.idiomatic: After ten years a monk opened a public hall nearby and the noise drove him back to Mirage Garden, where he lived by selling his writing;

sentences.zh: 不足，則與其妻為椶奚竹筥以佐之。

translations.literal: When insufficient, he and his wife made palm-fiber and bamboo hampers to supplement it.
translations.idiomatic: when that was not enough, he and his wife wove palm-fiber and bamboo baskets to make ends meet.

sentences.zh: 好事者約月供薪米，力辭不受。

translations.literal: Well-wishers arranged monthly supplies of fuel and grain; he strenuously declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Sympathizers offered him a monthly allowance of fuel and grain, but he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 有司慕其高，往訪之，輒踰垣避。

translations.literal: The magistrates admired his loftiness and went to visit; he would always climb over the wall to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials, admiring his integrity, came to call on him, but he would climb over the wall to get away.

sentences.zh: 所著詩文，皆吊甲申以來殉節者。

translations.literal: His poems and prose all mourn those who died for integrity since jiashen.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he wrote in verse or prose was an elegy for those who had died for the dynasty since 1644.

sentences.zh: 蜃園者，乍浦勝地，可望見海市者也。

translations.literal: Mirage Garden was a famous spot of Zhapu from which one could view the mirage city on the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Mirage Garden was a beauty spot at Zhapu where one could look out and see the phantom city rise on the sea.

sentences.zh: 又十年，家益困，鬻其園，寄身僧舍，戚友贖而歸之，始復與妻居，時年七十矣。

translations.literal: After another ten years the household grew more destitute; he sold the garden and lodged in a monks' quarters; relatives and friends redeemed it and returned it; he was then reunited with his wife in residence, at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later the family was poorer still; he sold the garden and moved into a monastery until kinsmen bought it back for him; only then did he and his wife live together again, he being seventy by then.

sentences.zh: 子震，亦棄諸生，非義一介不取。

translations.literal: His son Zhen also abandoned his student status and would not take a single coin that was not right.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen had also given up his degree candidacy and would not accept a single coin that was not earned honestly.

sentences.zh: 老夫婦白頭相對，時絕食，則歎曰：「吾生本贅耳，待盡而已。

translations.literal: The old couple faced each other with white heads; when food occasionally ran out they would sigh and say: "My life was superfluous from the start—I only await the end."
translations.idiomatic: The old couple sat white-haired face to face, and when food ran out they would sigh, "My life has been a burden from the first—I am only waiting for the end."

sentences.zh: 」有餽食者，非其人，終不受。

translations.literal: " When food was offered, if it was not from the right person he would never accept it in the end.
translations.idiomatic: If food was offered by someone he did not respect, he would refuse it to the end.

sentences.zh: 或問身後，曰：「楊王孫之葬，何必棺也！

translations.literal: When asked about after death he said: "Yang Wangsun's burial—why must there be a coffin!"
translations.idiomatic: Asked about his funeral, he said, "Like Yang Wangsun—what need of a coffin!"

sentences.zh: 又十年，蜃園僅存二楹，兩耳聾，又苦腹疾，終日仰臥。

translations.literal: After another ten years Mirage Garden had only two bays left; both ears were deaf and he also suffered abdominal illness, lying on his back all day.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years on, only two rooms of Mirage Garden remained; he was deaf in both ears, tormented by stomach trouble, and lay on his back all day.

sentences.zh: 客至，以粉版書相問荅。

translations.literal: When guests came he would write questions and answers on a chalk tablet.
translations.idiomatic: When visitors came he conversed with them by writing on a whitewashed board.

sentences.zh: 魏禧來自江西，造其廬，天植與之粉版，書竟，天植視姓字，則強起張目視之，泣，禧亦泣。

translations.literal: Wei Xi came from Jiangxi and visited his hut; Tianzhi gave him a chalk tablet; when the writing was finished Tianzhi looked at the surname and given name, then forced himself to rise and open his eyes to look, wept, and Xi also wept.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xi came from Jiangxi to his cottage; Tianzhi handed him a writing board, and when Xi had finished writing his name Tianzhi strained to open his eyes, looked hard at the signature, and wept—and Xi wept too.

sentences.zh: 時方絕糧，禧探囊得銀半兩贈之，五反不受，固以請，曰：「此非盜跖物也！

translations.literal: At the time they were utterly without grain; Xi took from his pouch half a tael of silver to give him; five times he refused; Xi pressed it firmly, saying: "This is not the property of Robber Zhi!"
translations.idiomatic: They had no grain at all; Xi found half a tael of silver in his purse and offered it, but Tianzhi refused five times until Xi insisted, "This is no robber's loot!"

sentences.zh: 」始納之。

translations.literal: " Only then did he accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did Tianzhi take it.

sentences.zh: 買米為炊，共食而別。

translations.literal: He bought rice and cooked; they ate together and parted.
translations.idiomatic: He bought rice, cooked a meal, they ate together, and parted.

sentences.zh: 禧囑布衣週篔、侍郎曹溶糾同志為繼粟，且謀身後事，徐枋聞之曰：「李先生不食人食，聽其以餓死可也。

translations.literal: Xi entrusted the commoner Zhou Yun and Vice Minister Cao Rong to gather like-minded men for continued grain supplies and also to plan posthumous affairs; Xu Fang heard of it and said: "Mr. Li does not eat other people's food—let him starve to death if he will."
translations.idiomatic: On leaving, Xi asked the scholar Zhou Yun and Vice Minister Cao Rong to organize friends to keep grain coming and to arrange his funeral; when Xu Fang heard of it he said, "Mr. Li will not eat another man's bread—let him starve if that is his wish."

sentences.zh: 」已而篔齎粟往，天植果堅拒。

translations.literal: " Before long Yun brought grain; Tianzhi indeed firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhou Yun arrived with grain, and Tianzhi refused it just as firmly.

sentences.zh: 禧聞之，曰：「吾淺之乎為丈夫已。

translations.literal: When Xi heard of it he said: "How shallow I was to act as a true man!"
translations.idiomatic: When Xi heard of this he said, "How shallow I was—thinking myself a man of principle!"

sentences.zh: 」乍浦有鄭嬰垣者，孤介絕俗，與天植稱金石交，先二年，凍死雪中，至是天植亦飢死。

translations.literal: " At Zhapu there was one Zheng Yingyuan, solitary and beyond convention, who with Tianzhi were styled friends as firm as metal and stone; two years earlier he had frozen to death in the snow; at this time Tianzhi also died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhapu there lived Zheng Yingyuan, proud and aloof; he and Tianzhi called each other friends of iron and stone. Two years earlier Zheng had frozen to death in the snow; now Tianzhi starved to death as well.

sentences.zh: 臨歾，曰：「吾無愧於老友矣！

translations.literal: On the verge of death he said: "I have no shame before my old friend!"
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he said, "I have nothing to be ashamed of before my old friend!"

sentences.zh: 」時康熙十一年也。

translations.literal: " It was then the eleventh year of Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: It was the eleventh year of the Kangxi reign.

sentences.zh: 年八十有二。

translations.literal: His age was eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 葬牛橋。

translations.literal: He was buried at Niuchiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried at Niuchiao.

sentences.zh: 所著有蜃園集、乍浦九山志。

translations.literal: His works include Collected Writings of Mirage Garden and Gazetteer of the Nine Mountains of Zhapu.
translations.idiomatic: His writings include the Collected Writings of Mirage Garden and the Gazetteer of the Nine Mountains of Zhapu.

sentences.zh: 理洪儲，字繼起，興化人。

translations.literal: Li Hongchu, courtesy name Jiaqi, was a native of Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chu, who bore the adopted surname Li and was styled Jiaqi, came from Xinghua; his birth name had been Li.

sentences.zh: 本姓李。

translations.literal: His original surname was Li.
translations.idiomatic: His family had originally been surnamed Li.

sentences.zh: 父嘉兆與中州理鬯和恥與賊同姓，​​皆改理氏，天下稱「二理」。

translations.literal: His father Jiazhao and Changhe of Zhongzhou in Henan, ashamed of sharing the bandits' surname, both changed to the Li clan; the realm called them "the Two Lis."
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiazhao and Li Changhe of the Central Plains, shamed at sharing the rebels' surname Li, both took the character Li instead; people called them "the Two Lis."

sentences.zh: 洪儲早歲出家，南都覆，明之遺臣多舉兵，洪儲左右之，被逮，獲免，好事如故。

translations.literal: Hong Chu left home early; when the Southern Capital fell, many remnant Ming ministers raised troops and Hong Chu assisted them; he was arrested but escaped punishment, and carried on as before.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Chu had entered the clergy in his youth; when Nanjing fell, many Ming loyalists took up arms and he aided them; he was arrested but released, and went on as before.

sentences.zh: 人戒之，則曰：「吾苟自反無媿，即有意外風波，久當自定。

translations.literal: When people warned him he would say: "If I examine myself and have no shame, even should there be unexpected storms, in time they will settle of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When people cautioned him he would say, "If I search my conscience and find no fault, then even if trouble comes out of nowhere, in time it will quiet down."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「憂患得其宜，湯火亦樂國也。

translations.literal: " He also said: "When distress and peril are fittingly borne, scalding water and fire are also a joyful realm."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "When hardship is met as it should be, even boiling water and fire are a happy land."

sentences.zh: 」枋聞之，歎曰：「是真能以忠孝作佛事者也！

translations.literal: " When Fang heard this he sighed and said: "This is truly one who can make Buddhist practice out of loyalty and filial piety!"
translations.idiomatic: When Fang heard this he sighed and said, "Here is a man who can truly turn loyalty and filial piety into Buddhist devotion!"

sentences.zh: 」洪儲在沙門，宏暢宗風，篤好人物，海內皆能道之。

translations.literal: " Hong Chu as a monk broadly spread the sect's wind and deeply cherished men of worth; within and beyond the seas all could speak of him.
translations.idiomatic: As a monk Hong Chu spread his school's teaching widely and cherished worthy men; everyone within the realm could tell you about him.

sentences.zh: 枋曰：「此其跡也，但觀其每年三月十九日素服焚香，北面揮涕，二十八年如一日，是何為者？

translations.literal: Fang said: "This is only his trace—but look at how every year on the nineteenth day of the third month he wears plain robes, burns incense, faces north and waves away tears, for twenty-eight years like a single day—what is that for?"
translations.idiomatic: Fang said, "That is only the surface—but watch him every year on the nineteenth of the third month, in plain dress, burning incense, facing north in tears, twenty-eight years without a break: what is that for, if not the anniversary of Chongzhen's death?"

sentences.zh: 顧柔謙，字剛中，無錫人，遷常熟。

translations.literal: Gu Rouqian, courtesy name Gangzhong, was a native of Wuxi, later moved to Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Rouqian, styled Gangzhong, was from Wuxi and later moved to Changshu.

sentences.zh: 幼遭家難，貲產皆盡。

translations.literal: In youth he met household calamity and property was all lost.
translations.idiomatic: In childhood his family suffered a catastrophe and lost everything.

sentences.zh: 嘗同兄出門遊，有數人擁之行，行乃擠大澤中。

translations.literal: Once he went out touring with his elder brother; several men surrounded them on the road; as they walked, they were forced into a great marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Once he went out with his elder brother. Several men surrounded them on the road and, as they walked, forced them into a great swamp.

sentences.zh: 母忽心動，急呼老僕往蹟之，得不死。

translations.literal: His mother suddenly felt her heart stir, urgently called an old servant to trace them, and they did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Their mother had a sudden premonition, sent an old servant after them in haste, and they were saved.

sentences.zh: 補弟子員。

translations.literal: He was appointed a student member.
translations.idiomatic: He qualified as a government student.

sentences.zh: 甲申之變，柔謙哀憤，往往形諸詩歌，讀者悲之。

translations.literal: At the change of jiashen, Rouqian's grief and anger often took form in poetry and song; readers were moved to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of 1644 his grief and rage poured into his poems, and readers wept over them.

sentences.zh: 不妄交遊，以父執師事馬士奇，而江陰黃毓祺、嘉定黃淳耀皆一見定交。

translations.literal: He did not associate casually; he treated Ma Shiji, his father's friend, as teacher, while Huang Yuqi of Jiangyin and Huang Chunyao of Jiading each became bound friends at a single meeting.
translations.idiomatic: He was choosy in friendship, honored his father's friend Ma Shiji as a teacher, and with Huang Yuqi of Jiangyin and Huang Chunyao of Jiading formed lifelong bonds at first meeting.

sentences.zh: 諸人殉國難，柔謙皆設位以哭盡哀。

translations.literal: When those men died for the national calamity, Rouqian in each case set out a seat and wept to the full of grief.
translations.idiomatic: When they died for the dynasty he set out mourning tablets for each and wept his fill.

sentences.zh: 子祖禹，見父嘗閉門嘿坐，或竟日不食，祖禹叩頭寬譬，柔謙乃曰：「汝能終身窮餓，不思富貴乎？

translations.literal: His son Zuyu, seeing his father sometimes shut the door and sit in silence, or go a whole day without eating, Zuyu knocked his head in comfort and persuasion; Rouqian then said: "Can you spend your life in poverty and hunger, not thinking of wealth and honor?"
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuyu once found him shut indoors, sitting in silence, having eaten nothing all day; Zuyu kowtowed and tried to comfort him, and Rouqian said, "Could you live poor and hungry all your life and never dream of riches?"

sentences.zh: 」祖禹跪應曰：「能。

translations.literal: " Zuyu knelt and answered: "I can."
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu knelt and answered, "I could."

sentences.zh: 」柔謙曰：「汝能以身為人機上肉，不思報復乎？

translations.literal: " Rouqian said: "Can you make your body meat on another's chopping block and not think of revenge?"
translations.idiomatic: Rouqian asked, "Could you let yourself be meat on the block and never think of revenge?"

sentences.zh: 」祖禹复應曰：「能。

translations.literal: " Zuyu again answered: "I can."
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu answered again, "I could."

sentences.zh: 」柔謙喜曰：「吾與汝偕隱耳！

translations.literal: " Rouqian rejoiced and said: "You and I shall withdraw together!"
translations.idiomatic: Rouqian said gladly, "Then you and I will live in seclusion together!"

sentences.zh: 」遂更名隱，署其室曰伐檀。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he changed his name to Yin and titled his chamber Felling Sandalwood.
translations.idiomatic: He changed his son's name to Yin and named his study "Felling Sandalwood."

sentences.zh: 常夜蹴祖禹曰：「汝他日得志，如舊怨何？

translations.literal: He would often at night kick Zuyu and say: "If you one day attain your aim, what of old grievances?"
translations.idiomatic: He would often wake Zuyu at night and ask, "If you rise in the world someday, what will you do about our old enemies?"

sentences.zh: 」祖禹曰：「每憶幼時祖母抱兒置膝上，為言家難，及墮大澤中事，祖禹不敢忘。

translations.literal: " Zuyu said: "Whenever I recall how in childhood Grandmother held me on her knee and spoke of the household calamity and the matter of falling into the great marsh, I dare not forget."
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu said, "I still remember Grandmother holding me on her knee as a boy and telling me about the family tragedy and how we were driven into the swamp—I cannot forget."

sentences.zh: 」柔謙曰：「嘻，汝何見之隘？

translations.literal: " Rouqian said: "Alas, how narrow is your view!"
translations.idiomatic: Rouqian said, "Tsk—you take too small a view!"

sentences.zh: 吾家數傳以來，頗盈盛，以祖、父之才，而竟中折，天也！

translations.literal: Our house for several generations has been rather flourishing; with grandfather's and father's talents, yet in the end cut off midway—this is Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Our family had flourished for generations; with the talents of your grandfather and father we should have prospered—yet we were cut down midway. That was Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 於彼何尤？

translations.literal: What blame toward them?
translations.idiomatic: What grievance can we hold against those men?

sentences.zh: 同室之中，寧彼以非禮來，吾不可以非禮報，汝謹識之！

translations.literal: Within the same household, better that they come with impropriety than that we answer with impropriety—you must keep this firmly in mind!
translations.idiomatic: Under one roof, let them act without propriety if they will—we must not answer in kind. Remember that!

sentences.zh: 」著有補韻略、六書考定、山居贅論。

translations.literal: " His works include Supplement to Rhymes in Brief, Examination and Fixation of the Six Scripts, and Miscellaneous Discourses from Mountain Dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: His books include the Supplement to Rhymes in Brief, the Examination and Fixation of the Six Scripts, and Miscellaneous Discourses from Mountain Dwelling.

sentences.zh: 祖禹，字復初。

translations.literal: Zuyu, styled Fuchu.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu, whose courtesy name was Fuchu.

sentences.zh: 柔謙精於史學，嘗謂：「明一統志於戰守攻取之要，類皆不詳山川，條列又復割裂失倫，源流不備。

translations.literal: Rouqian was skilled in historical studies and once said: "In the Ming Comprehensive Gazetteer, on the essentials of defense, attack, and warfare, mountains and rivers are mostly not detailed; when set out in entries they are again cut apart and lose order, and streams and sources are incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Rouqian was a fine historian and once remarked, "In the Ming dynasty's Comprehensive Gazetteer, the points that matter for war, defense, and conquest rarely give proper detail on terrain; the entries are chopped apart so the scheme falls apart, and the courses of rivers are left incomplete.

sentences.zh: 」祖禹承其志，撰讀史方輿紀要一百三十卷，凡職方、廣輿諸書，承譌襲謬，皆為駮正。

translations.literal: " Zuyu took up his intent and compiled Essentials of Historical Geography in one hundred thirty juan; wherever books such as Directorate of Works and Broad Geography carried on errors and repeated mistakes, he refuted and corrected them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu took up that aim and wrote the Essentials of Historical Geography in one hundred thirty juan, rebutting and correcting every error handed down in such works as the Directorate of Works records and the Broad Geography.

sentences.zh: 詳於山川險易，及古今戰守成敗之跡，而景物名勝皆在所略。

translations.literal: It is detailed on the difficulty and ease of mountains and rivers and on traces of success and failure in warfare ancient and modern, while scenic spots and famous sites are all omitted.
translations.idiomatic: It is rich on terrain and on the record of battles won and lost through the ages, but famous views and scenic sites are deliberately left out.

sentences.zh: 創稿時年二十九，及成書，年五十矣。

translations.literal: When he began the draft he was twenty-nine; when the book was finished he was fifty.
translations.idiomatic: He started the manuscript at twenty-nine and was fifty when it was complete.

sentences.zh: 寧都魏禧見之，歎曰：「此數千百年絕無僅有之書也！

translations.literal: Wei Xi of Ningdu saw it and sighed: "This is a book without parallel in several thousand years!
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Xi of Ningdu saw it he exclaimed, "In thousands of years there has never been a book like this!

sentences.zh: 」以其書與梅文鼎曆算全書、李清南北史合鈔稱三大奇書。

translations.literal: " He ranked this book with Mei Wending's Complete Works on Calendar and Mathematics and Li Qing's Collated Northern and Southern Histories as the three great marvel-books.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked it with Mei Wending's Complete Works on Calendar and Mathematics and Li Qing's Collated Northern and Southern Histories as the three supreme oddities among books.

sentences.zh: 祖禹與禧為金石交，禧客死，祖禹經紀其喪。

translations.literal: Zuyu and Xi had a bond firm as metal and stone; when Xi died far from home, Zuyu managed his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Zuyu and Xi were friends as close as metal and stone; when Xi died away from home, Zuyu arranged his burial.

sentences.zh: 徐乾學奉敕修一統志，延致祖禹，將薦起之，力亂罷。

translations.literal: Xu Qianxue received orders to compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer, invited Zuyu, and was about to recommend him for office, but because of the turmoil it was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Qianxue was ordered to compile the Comprehensive Gazetteer, brought Zuyu in, and was ready to recommend him back into service, but the disorder put an end to it.

sentences.zh: 後終於​​家。

translations.literal: Later he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he died at home.

sentences.zh: 冒襄，字辟疆，別號巢民，如皋人。

translations.literal: Mao Xiang, styled Bijiang, alias Chaomin, a native of Rugao.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiang, courtesy name Bijiang, also called Chaomin, was from Rugao.

sentences.zh: 父起宗，明副使。

translations.literal: His father Qizong was a vice commissioner of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qizong had been a Ming vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 襄十歲能詩，董其昌為作序。

translations.literal: At ten Xiang could compose poetry, and Dong Qichang wrote a preface for him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang could write poetry at ten, and Dong Qichang composed a preface for him.

sentences.zh: 崇禎壬午副榜貢生，當授推官，會亂作，遂不出。

translations.literal: In the renchen year of Chongzhen he ranked on the provincial supplemental list as a tribute student and was to be appointed push-official, but rebellion broke out and he did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen renchen year he placed on the provincial supplemental list and was due to receive a push-official appointment, but upheaval broke out and he never took office.

sentences.zh: 與桐城方以智、宜興陳貞慧、商丘侯方域，並稱「四公子」。

translations.literal: With Fang Yizhi of Tongcheng, Chen Zhenhui of Yixing, and Hou Fangyu of Shangqiu, they were together called the "Four Gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: Together with Fang Yizhi of Tongcheng, Chen Zhenhui of Yixing, and Hou Fangyu of Shangqiu, he was known as one of the "Four Gentlemen."

sentences.zh: 襄少年負盛氣，才特高，尤能傾動人。

translations.literal: In youth Xiang bore fierce pride; his talent was exceptionally high, and above all he could move people.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Xiang was proud and high-spirited, his gifts extraordinary, and he had a gift above all for swaying others.

sentences.zh: 嘗置酒桃葉渡，會六君子諸孤，一時名士咸集。

translations.literal: Once he set wine at Taoye Ford and gathered the orphaned sons of the Six Gentlemen; famous men of the day all assembled.
translations.idiomatic: He once held a feast at Taoye Ford for the orphaned sons of the Six Gentlemen, and every notable of the day came.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，輒發狂悲歌，訾詈懷寧阮大鋮，大鋮故奄黨也。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep he would break into wild lament and song, reviling Huaining Ruan Dacheng—Dacheng was of the eunuch faction.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was deep he would sing wildly in grief and revile Ruan Dacheng of Huaining, who had belonged to the eunuch faction.

sentences.zh: 時金陵歌舞諸部，以懷寧為冠，歌詞皆出大鋮。

translations.literal: At the time the singing troupes of Jinling, with Huaining foremost, had lyrics all from Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Then the song companies of Jinling, with Huaining's troupe at the head, sang lyrics that all came from Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 大鋮欲自結諸社人，令歌者來，襄與客且罵且稱善，大鋮聞之益恨。

translations.literal: Dacheng wished to attach himself to the literary society men and sent singers; Xiang and his guests cursed yet also praised the performance, and Dacheng hearing it hated all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Dacheng tried to win over the literary men and sent singers; Xiang and his guests cursed them even as they praised the songs, and Dacheng hated him all the more when he heard of it.

sentences.zh: 甲申黨獄興，襄賴救僅免。

translations.literal: In jiashen the faction cases arose; Xiang escaped harm only by rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When the jiashen faction persecutions broke out, Xiang was spared only because others saved him.

sentences.zh: 家故有園池亭館之勝，歸益喜客，招致無虛日，家自此中落，怡然不悔也。

translations.literal: His house had long had fine gardens, pools, pavilions, and lodges; after returning he delighted all the more in guests and entertained without a vacant day—the family from this declined to ruin, yet he was content and unregretful.
translations.idiomatic: The family estate had fine gardens and halls; after he withdrew he entertained guests every day without pause, and though the household sank into poverty he was cheerful and never sorry.

sentences.zh: 襄既隱居不出，名益盛。

translations.literal: After Xiang had withdrawn and would not come forth, his fame grew greater.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiang lived in seclusion and refused office, his reputation only grew.

sentences.zh: 督撫以監軍薦，御史以人才薦，皆以親老辭。

translations.literal: Governors and grand coordinators recommended him to supervise armies; censors recommended him as talent—but he declined each on grounds that his parents were aged.
translations.idiomatic: Governors recommended him to oversee troops and censors recommended him as talent, but he refused each time, pleading aged parents.

sentences.zh: 康熙中，復以山林隱逸及博學鴻詞薦，亦不就。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi reign he was again recommended as a hermit of mountain and forest and for Erudite Learning and Polished Composition, yet he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kangxi he was again put forward as a mountain recluse and for the Erudite Learning and Polished Composition examination, and again he would not go.

sentences.zh: 著述甚富，行世者，有先世前徽錄，六十年師友詩文同人集，樸巢詩文集，水繪園詩文集。

translations.literal: His writings were very abundant; those in circulation include Records of Ancestral Excellence, Collected Works of Masters and Friends over Sixty Years, Collected Poems and Prose of the Rustic Nest, and Collected Poems and Prose of the Water-Painted Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote copiously; works that circulated include Records of Ancestral Excellence, Collected Writings of Masters and Friends over Sixty Years, the Rustic Nest collection, and the Water-Painted Garden collection.

sentences.zh: 書法絕妙，喜作擘大字，人皆藏★M8珍之。

translations.literal: His calligraphy was superb; he loved writing large split-stroke characters, and everyone treasured and cherished them.
translations.idiomatic: His calligraphy was superb; he loved writing large split-stroke characters, and everyone hoarded them as treasures.

sentences.zh: 康熙三十二年，卒，年八十有三。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi he died, aged eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year of Kangxi he died at the age of eighty-three.

sentences.zh: 私諡潛孝先生。

translations.literal: His private posthumous title was Master Qianxiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the private posthumous title Master Qianxiao.

sentences.zh: 陳貞慧，字定生，宜興人，明都御史陳於廷子。

translations.literal: Chen Zhenhui, styled Dingsheng, a native of Yixing, son of Ming censor-in-chief Chen Yuting.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhenhui, courtesy name Dingsheng, was from Yixing and was the son of the Ming censor-in-chief Chen Yuting.

sentences.zh: 於廷，東林黨魁。

translations.literal: Yuting was leader of the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuting had been a leader of the Donglin faction.

sentences.zh: 貞慧與吳應箕草留都防亂檄，擯阮大鋮。

translations.literal: Zhenhui and Wu Yingji drafted a manifesto at Nanjing to prevent disorder, excluding Ruan Dacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenhui and Wu Yingji drafted the Nanjing manifesto against disorder, which shut out Ruan Dacheng.

sentences.zh: 黨禍起，逮貞慧至鎮撫司，事雖解，已瀕十死。

translations.literal: When the faction disaster arose Zhenhui was seized to the Pacification Office; though the affair was resolved he had nearly died ten deaths.
translations.idiomatic: When the faction disaster broke out he was taken to the Pacification Office; though the case was settled he had been within a hair's breadth of death many times over.

sentences.zh: 國亡，埋身土室，不入城市者十餘年。

translations.literal: When the dynasty fell he buried himself in an earthen chamber and did not enter the city for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he shut himself in an earthen room and stayed out of the cities for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 遺民故老時時向陽羨山中一問生死，流連痛飲，驚離吊往，聞者悲之。

translations.literal: Survivors and old friends would from time to time come to Yangxian mountain to ask after life and death; they lingered and drank in grief, startled by parting and mourning the gone—those who heard were saddened.
translations.idiomatic: Former subjects and old friends would climb to Yangxian mountain to ask how he fared; they drank long in grief, startled by partings and mourning the dead, and those who heard it were moved to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 順

translations.literal: Shun-
translations.idiomatic: In the Shunzhi reign,

sentences.zh: 治十三年，卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: zhi thirteenth year, he died, aged fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: in the thirteenth year he died, aged fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 著有皇明語林、山陽錄、雪岑集、交遊錄、秋園雜佩諸書。

translations.literal: His works include Imperial Ming Conversations, Records of Shanyang, Collected Snow at the Hill Crest, Record of Associates, and Miscellaneous Adornments of the Autumn Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Imperial Ming Conversations, Records of Shanyang, Collected Snow at the Hill Crest, Record of Associates, and Miscellaneous Adornments of the Autumn Garden, among other books.

sentences.zh: 子維崧，見文苑傳。

translations.literal: His son Weisong is treated in the Literary Grove biography.
translations.idiomatic: His son Weisong is discussed in the Literary Grove biography.

sentences.zh: 祁班孫，字奕喜，山陰人。

translations.literal: Qi Bansun, styled Yixi, a native of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Bansun, courtesy name Yixi, was from Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 父彪佳，明蘇松巡撫。

translations.literal: His father Biaojia was Ming governor of Jiangsu and Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Biaojia had been Ming governor of Jiangsu and Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 班孫次六，人稱六公子，彪佳嘗受業於劉宗周，宗周將兵江上，班孫與其兄理孫罄家餉之。

translations.literal: Bansun was sixth-born and called the Sixth Gentleman; Biaojia had studied under Liu Zongzhou, and when Zongzhou led troops on the river Bansun and his elder brother Lisun exhausted the family fortune to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: Bansun was the sixth son and known as the Sixth Gentleman; Biaojia had studied under Liu Zongzhou, and when Zongzhou raised troops on the river Bansun and his elder brother Lisun spent the family fortune to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 祁氏藏書甲江左，班孫兄弟以故國喬木自任。

translations.literal: The Qi family's book collection ranked first in Jiangzuo; the Bansun brothers took upon themselves the role of surviving trees of the former dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi library was the finest east of the Yangtze; the brothers held themselves like the last great trees of the fallen dynasty.

sentences.zh: 豪宕喜結客，家居山陰之梅墅，園林深茂。

translations.literal: Bold and expansive, he loved gathering clients; his home was at Meisha in Shanyin, with deep gardens and thick groves.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and loved to gather clients; he lived at Meisha in Shanyin in gardens deep and woods thick.

sentences.zh: 登其堂，複壁大隧，莫能詰也。

translations.literal: When one entered his hall, double walls and great tunnels—none could interrogate them.
translations.idiomatic: Inside his hall were double walls and long tunnels, and no one could trace them.

sentences.zh: 慈谿布衣魏耕者，狂走四方，思得一當。

translations.literal: Wei Geng, a commoner of Cixi, ran wild through the four quarters, seeking one decisive stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Geng, a commoner of Cixi, roamed the realm in reckless hope of one decisive blow.

sentences.zh: 班孫兄弟與之誓天，稱莫逆。

translations.literal: The Bansun brothers swore oaths to Heaven with him and called themselves sworn friends.
translations.idiomatic: The Bansun brothers swore oaths with him before Heaven and called themselves his sworn friends.

sentences.zh: 或告變於浙大吏，四道捕耕，並縛班孫兄弟去。

translations.literal: Someone reported a plot to the great official of Zhejiang; four roads arrested Geng and bound the Bansun brothers away.
translations.idiomatic: Someone denounced the plot to the Zhejiang authorities; troops on four routes seized Geng and took the brothers away in bonds.

sentences.zh: 既讞，兄弟爭承，祁氏客乃納賂而宥其兄。

translations.literal: After judgment the brothers contended to take responsibility; then a Qi family guest paid bribes and pardoned the elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: After the verdict the brothers each tried to claim guilt, until a Qi family guest paid bribes and won pardon for the elder brother.

sentences.zh: 班孫遣戍遼左，理孫竟以痛弟鬱鬱死，而祁氏家亦破。

translations.literal: Bansun was sent to garrison the Liaodong left; Lisun in the end died of grief for his brother, and the Qi household was also ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Bansun was exiled to the left wing of Liaodong; Lisun died of grief for his brother, and the Qi house was broken.

sentences.zh: 旋班孫遁歸，祝髮於吳之堯峰，尋主毗陵馬鞍山寺，所稱咒林明大師者也。

translations.literal: Before long Bansun fled back, tonsured at Yao Peak in Wu, then became abbot of Ma'an Mountain Temple in Piling—he whom they called Master Mingda of Zhoulin.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bansun escaped home, shaved his head at Yao Peak in Wu, and later headed Ma'an Mountain Temple in Piling, known as Master Mingda of Zhoulin.

sentences.zh: 班孫好議​​論古今，不談佛法，每語及先朝，則掩面哭，然終莫有知之者。

translations.literal: Bansun loved discussing past and present but did not speak of Buddhist law; whenever he came to the former dynasty he covered his face and wept, yet in the end none knew him.
translations.idiomatic: Bansun loved to debate past and present and never spoke of Buddhist doctrine; whenever the former dynasty was mentioned he hid his face and wept, yet in the end no one knew who he had been.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 發其篋，有東行風俗記、紫芝軒集。

translations.literal: When they opened his casket they found Record of Eastern Travel Customs and Collected Works of the Purple Polypore Studio.
translations.idiomatic: When his box was opened they found the Record of Eastern Travel Customs and the Purple Polypore Studio collection.

sentences.zh: 且得其遺教，命歸祔，乃知為山陰祁六公子，遂得返葬雲。

translations.literal: And they obtained his last instruction ordering bones returned for joint burial, and then knew he was the Sixth Gentleman Qi of Shanyin, and were able to return him for burial at Yun.
translations.idiomatic: They also found his last testament bidding his bones be brought home for burial, and only then learned he was the Sixth Gentleman Qi of Shanyin, so he could be returned and buried at Yun.

sentences.zh: 班孫娶少師硃燮元女孫，硃工詩。

translations.literal: Bansun married the granddaughter of Junior Tutor Zhu Xieyuan; Zhu was skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Bansun married the granddaughter of Junior Tutor Zhu Xieyuan, who was herself a fine poet.

sentences.zh: 其來歸也，與其姑商、姒張、小姑湘君，時相唱和。

translations.literal: When she came home in marriage, with her aunt-in-law Shang, sister-in-law Zhang, and young aunt Xiangjun they often exchanged poems.
translations.idiomatic: When she came to the household she often exchanged poems with her aunt-in-law Shang, her sister-in-law Zhang, and her young aunt Xiangjun.

sentences.zh: 商氏字塚婦曰楚纕，字介婦曰趙璧，以志閨門之盛。

translations.literal: The Shang women—the eldest daughter-in-law was styled Chuxiang, the second Zhuozhao—thus to record the glory of the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Shang women took styles for the household: the eldest daughter-in-law was called Chuxiang and the second Zhuozhao, to mark the splendor of the women's quarters.

sentences.zh: 班孫既被難，硃盛年，孤燈緇帳，數十年未嘗一出廳屏。

translations.literal: After Bansun met disaster Zhu was in the prime of life; alone by lamp in black gauze, for decades she never once passed the hall screen.
translations.idiomatic: After Bansun's disaster Zhu was still young; for decades by a lone lamp in mourning dress she never once stepped beyond the hall screen.

sentences.zh: 自班孫兄弟歾，淡生堂書星散，論者謂江東文獻一大厄運也。

translations.literal: After the Bansun brothers died the Dansheng Hall books scattered like stars; commentators called it a great catastrophe for the literary legacies of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bansun brothers were gone the Dansheng Hall library scattered like stars, and writers called it a great blow to Jiangdong's literary heritage.

sentences.zh: 汪渢，字魏美，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Wang Feng, styled Weimei, a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Feng, courtesy name Weimei, was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 少孤貧，力學，與人落落寡諧，人號曰汪冷。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and poor, he strove in learning; with others he was remote and rarely harmonious—people called him Cold Wang.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, he studied hard; aloof and hard to get along with, people nicknamed him Cold Wang.

sentences.zh: 舉崇禎己卯鄉試，與同縣陸培齊名。

translations.literal: In the jimao year of Chongzhen he passed the provincial examination, famed alongside Lu Pei of the same county.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen jimao year he passed the provincial examination and was famed alongside Lu Pei of the same county.

sentences.zh: 甲申後，培自經死，渢為文祭之，一慟幾絕，遂棄科舉。

translations.literal: After jiashen Pei hanged himself; Feng wrote a mourning piece for him, wept until nearly unconscious, and abandoned the examination track.
translations.idiomatic: After jiashen Pei hanged himself; Feng wrote a funeral elegy for him, wept until he nearly fainted, and gave up the examination path forever.

sentences.zh: ★L5黨欲強之試禮部，出千金兒其妻，俾勸駕，妻曰：「吾夫子不可勸，吾亦不屑此金也。
