translations.literal: The ★L5 faction wished to force him to take the metropolitan examination, offered a thousand gold to bribe his wife to urge him on—his wife said: "My husband cannot be urged, and I too disdain this gold.
translations.idiomatic: The ★L5 party tried to force him into the metropolitan examination, offering a thousand in gold to bribe his wife to persuade him; she said, "My husband cannot be persuaded, and I scorn this gold as well.

sentences.zh: 」嘗獨身提藥裹往來山谷間，宿食無定處。

translations.literal: " He would often go alone carrying medicine bundles through mountain valleys, with no fixed place for lodging or food.
translations.idiomatic: He often went alone with medicine bundles through mountain valleys, with no fixed lodging or meal.

sentences.zh: 渢故城居，母老，欲時時見渢，其兄澄、弟澐亦棄諸生服，奉母徙城外。

translations.literal: Feng had long lived in the city; his mother was old and wished to see Feng often; his elder brother Cheng and younger brother Yun also cast off licentiate status and moved with their mother outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Feng had lived in the city, but his mother was old and wanted to see him often; his elder brother Cheng and younger brother Yun also left off their student status and moved with her outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 渢時來定省，然渢能自來，家人欲往蹟之，不可得。

translations.literal: Feng would come at times to pay respects, but though Feng could come on his own, when family wished to trace him they could not find him.
translations.idiomatic: Feng would visit to pay his respects, yet though he could come of his own accord, when his kin tried to follow him they could not find him.

sentences.zh: 嗣因兵亂，奉母入天台。

translations.literal: Later because of military chaos he took his mother into Tiantai.
translations.idiomatic: Later, amid the wars, he brought his mother into Tiantai.

sentences.zh: 海上師起，群盜滿山谷，復返錢塘。

translations.literal: When armies rose on the sea and bandits filled the valleys, they returned to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: When coastal armies rose and bandits filled the hills, they returned to Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 當是時，湖上有三孝廉，皆高士，渢其一也，當事皆重之。

translations.literal: At that time there were three filial scholars on the lake, all lofty men—Feng was one—and officials all esteemed them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time three filial scholars lived on the lake, all men of high principle; Feng was one, and officials all honored them.

sentences.zh: 監司盧高尤下士，一日，遇渢於僧舍，問：「汪孝廉何在？

translations.literal: Commissioner Lu Gao especially honored scholars; one day meeting Feng in a monastery he asked: "Where is Filial Scholar Wang?
translations.idiomatic: The surveillance commissioner Lu Gao especially honored scholars; one day he met Feng in a monastery and asked, "Where is Filial Scholar Wang?

sentences.zh: 」渢應曰：「適在此，今已去矣。

translations.literal: Feng answered: "He was just here and has already left.
translations.idiomatic: Feng replied, "He was just here, but has already gone.

sentences.zh: 」高悵然，不知應者即渢也。

translations.literal: Gao sighed regretfully, not knowing the responder was Feng himself.
translations.idiomatic: Gao sighed in disappointment, not knowing the man who answered was Feng himself.

sentences.zh: 高嘗艤舟載酒西湖上，約三高士以世外禮相見，惟渢不至。

translations.literal: Gao once moored his boat and carried wine on West Lake, arranging to meet the three lofty men with worldly courtesy—only Feng did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Gao once anchored on West Lake with wine and arranged to meet the three recluses with the courtesy due men beyond the world, but Feng alone did not appear.

sentences.zh: 已，知其在孤山，以船就之，排牆遁去。

translations.literal: Later knowing he was at Solitary Hill, he took a boat to him; Feng slipped out through a gap in the wall and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned Feng was at Solitary Hill he went by boat to fetch him, but Feng slipped out through a breach in the wall and escaped.

sentences.zh: 渢不入城市，有司或以俸金為壽，不得卻，坎而埋之。

translations.literal: Feng did not enter the city; when officials sometimes sent stipends as birthday gifts he could not refuse outright but buried them in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: Feng would not enter the city; when officials sent salary as a birthday gift he could not send it back, so he buried it in a pit.

sentences.zh: 裡貴人請墓銘，饋百金，拒弗納。

translations.literal: When local magnates asked him to write epitaphs and offered a hundred gold, he refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: When local magnates asked for tomb inscriptions and offered a hundred in gold, he refused.

sentences.zh: 徙居孤山，匡床布被外，殘書數卷，鍵戶出，或返或不返，莫可踪跡。

translations.literal: He moved to Solitary Hill; besides a camp bed and cotton quilt he had only a few tattered books—locking the door he would go out and sometimes return or not, with no track to be found.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Solitary Hill with nothing but a camp bed, a cotton quilt, and a few worn books; he would lock the door and go away, sometimes returning and sometimes not, and no one could trace him.

sentences.zh: 遇好友，飲酒一斗不醉。

translations.literal: Meeting good friends he could drink a dou without getting drunk.
translations.idiomatic: With close friends he could drink a gallon and not show it.

sentences.zh: 晚好道，夜觀天象，晝習壬遁，能數日不食，了不問世事。

translations.literal: In later years he loved the Way; at night he observed heavenly signs, by day practiced Ren Dun, could go days without eating, and paid no heed to worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he turned to the Way: at night he watched the stars, by day he practiced Ren Dun divination, could fast for days, and cared nothing for worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 黃宗羲遇之於孤山，講龍溪調息法。

translations.literal: Huang Zongxi met him at Solitary Hill and discussed Longxi breath-regulation method.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi met him on Solitary Hill and they discussed the Longxi method of breath regulation.

sentences.zh: 嘗坐月至三更，夜寒甚，止布被一，渢與宗羲背相摩，得少暖氣。

translations.literal: Once they sat until the third watch of the night; it was very cold—only one cotton quilt; Feng and Zongxi rubbed backs to gain a little warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Once they sat talking until the third watch; the night was bitterly cold and they had only one cotton quilt, so Feng and Zongxi pressed their backs together for a little warmth.

sentences.zh: 魏禧自江西來訪，謝弗見。

translations.literal: Wei Xi came from Jiangxi to visit; Feng declined to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xi came from Jiangxi to call on him, but Feng refused to receive him.

sentences.zh: 禧留書曰：「吾寧都魏禧也，欲與子握手一痛哭耳！

translations.literal: Xi left a note: "I am Wei Xi of Ningdu; I wish to grasp your hand and weep together once!
translations.idiomatic: Xi left a note: "I am Wei Xi of Ningdu; I only want to take your hand and weep with you once!

sentences.zh: 」渢省書大驚，一見若平生歡。

translations.literal: Feng read the note and was greatly startled; on meeting they were as glad as lifelong friends.
translations.idiomatic: Feng read the note and was deeply moved; when they met they rejoiced like old friends of a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 臨別，執手涕下。

translations.literal: At parting they held hands and wept.
translations.idiomatic: When they parted they clasped hands and wept.

sentences.zh: 渢嘗從愚菴和尚究出世法，禧曰：「君事愚菴謹，豈有意為其弟子耶？

translations.literal: Feng had once studied the path beyond the world with Master Yu'an; Xi said: "You serve Yu'an with care—do you mean to become his disciple?
translations.idiomatic: Feng had once studied the way of release with Master Yu'an; Xi said, "You serve Yu'an devotedly—do you mean to become his disciple?

sentences.zh: 」渢曰：「吾甚敬愚菴，然今之志士，多為釋氏牽去，此吾所以不屑也。

translations.literal: Feng said: "I greatly respect Yu'an, but many men of ambition today are drawn away by Buddhism—that is why I disdain it.
translations.idiomatic: Feng said, "I respect Yu'an deeply, but too many men of spirit today are pulled away by Buddhism, and that is why I will not follow it.

sentences.zh: 」康熙四年秋，終於寶石山僧舍，年四十有八。

translations.literal: In autumn of the fourth year of Kangxi he died at a monastic lodge on Baoshi Mountain, aged forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Kangxi's fourth year he died in a monk's lodge on Baoshi Mountain, aged forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 臨歾，舉書卷焚之，詩文無一存者。

translations.literal: As he was dying he took up scrolls of writing and burned them; not a line of poetry or prose remained.
translations.idiomatic: As death approached he burned his manuscripts, and not a poem or essay was left.

sentences.zh: 起視日影，曰：「可矣！

translations.literal: Raising his eyes to the sun's shadow he said: "It will do!
translations.idiomatic: He looked at the sun's shadow and said, "That will do!

sentences.zh: 」書五言詩一章，投筆就寢而逝。

translations.literal: He wrote one stanza of five-character verse, cast down the brush, lay down, and passed away.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote a five-character quatrain, set down the brush, lay down, and died.

sentences.zh: 渢與陳廷會、柴紹炳、沈昀、孫治人，稱「西陵五君子」。

translations.literal: Feng with Chen Tinghui, Chai Shaobin, Shen Yun, and Sun Zhi were called the "Five Gentlemen of Xiling."
translations.idiomatic: Feng, together with Chen Tinghui, Chai Shaobin, Shen Yun, and Sun Zhi, was known as one of the "Five Gentlemen of Xiling."

sentences.zh: 餘增遠，字謙貞，世稱若水先生，會稽人。

translations.literal: Yu Zengyuan, styled Qianzhen, commonly called Master Ruoshui, a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Zengyuan, courtesy name Qianzhen, known as Master Ruoshui, was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎十六年進士，除寶應知縣。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen of Ming he became a jinshi and was appointed magistrate of Baoying.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Chongzhen he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed magistrate of Baoying.

sentences.zh: 南都授禮部主事，遷郎中。

translations.literal: At the Southern Capital he was made a director in the Ministry of Rites and promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: At the Southern Capital he was made a director in the Ministry of Rites and then promoted to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 事敗，逃之山中。

translations.literal: When the cause failed he fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When the cause was lost he fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 郡縣逼之出見，乃輿疾城南，以死拒。

translations.literal: The prefecture and county pressed him to come out and be seen; he then feigned illness south of the city and refused with death.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture and county pressed him to appear; he then had himself carried ill to the south of the city and resisted with his life.

sentences.zh: 久之，事得解。

translations.literal: After a long while the affair was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: In time the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 草屋三間，不蔽風雨，以鱉甲承漏。

translations.literal: Three thatched rooms, not sheltering from wind and rain; turtle shells caught the leaks.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in three thatched rooms that could not keep out wind and rain, and used turtle shells to catch the dripping.

sentences.zh: 聚村童五六人，授以三字經。

translations.literal: He gathered five or six village children and taught them the Three-Character Classic.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered five or six village children and taught them the Three-Character Classic.

sentences.zh: 臥榻之下，牛宮雞，無下足處。

translations.literal: Under his couch were ox pens and chicken coops, with no place to set a foot down.
translations.idiomatic: Ox stalls and chicken coops crowded beneath his bed, leaving no room to put his feet down.

sentences.zh: 晨則秉耒出，與老農雜作。

translations.literal: In the morning he took up his hoe and went out, working mixed among old farmers.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he took up his hoe and went out to labor alongside the old farmers.

sentences.zh: 同年生王天錫為海防道，欲與話舊，以疾辭。

translations.literal: A fellow graduate, Wang Tianxi, served as maritime defense intendant; wishing to renew old acquaintance, Zengyuan declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: His fellow graduate Wang Tianxi, who served as maritime defense intendant, wished to renew their old friendship, but Zengyuan declined, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 天錫披帷直入，增遠擁衾不起，曰：「不幸有狗馬疾，不得與故人為禮。

translations.literal: Tianxi brushed aside the curtain and entered straight in; Zengyuan wrapped himself in his quilt and would not rise, saying: "Unfortunately I have a dog-or-horse illness and cannot perform the rites due an old friend.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi brushed aside the curtain and walked straight in. Zengyuan pulled his quilt around him and would not rise, saying, "I am afflicted, alas, with a common ailment, and cannot perform the courtesies owed an old friend.

sentences.zh: 」天錫執手勞苦，出間未數武，則已與一婢子擔糞灌園矣。

translations.literal: " Tianxi took his hand in sympathy; before he had gone a few paces beyond the door, Zengyuan was already carrying night soil with a maid to water the garden.
translations.idiomatic: " Tianxi clasped his hand in concern and took his leave; he had not gone more than a few paces when Zengyuan was already carrying night soil with a maid to water the garden.

sentences.zh: 天賜遙望見之，嘆息去。

translations.literal: Tiansi saw this from afar and departed with a sigh.
translations.idiomatic: Watching from afar, Tiansi saw this and left with a sigh.

sentences.zh: 冬夏一皁帽，雖至暱者，不見其科頭。

translations.literal: Winter and summer one black cap; even those most intimate never saw him bareheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Winter and summer he wore a single black cap; even his closest intimates never saw him with his head uncovered.

sentences.zh: 增遠慨世路偪仄，遂疑荀卿性惡之說為確，至欲著論以非孟。

translations.literal: Zengyuan lamented the cramped path of the world, and came to suspect that Xunzi's doctrine of evil human nature was correct, even intending to write a treatise to refute Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: Zengyuan grieved that the ways of the world had grown narrow, and came to believe Xunzi's teaching that human nature is evil; he even intended to write a treatise against Mencius.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，卒，年六十有五。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he died, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Kangxi reign he died, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 蓋二十有四年不出城南一​​步也。

translations.literal: For twenty-four years he had not taken a single step south of the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: For twenty-four years he had not taken a single step south of the city wall.

sentences.zh: 疾革，黃宗羲造其榻前，欲為切脈，增遠笑曰：「某祈死二十年前，反祈生二十年後乎？

translations.literal: When his illness was critical, Huang Zongxi came to his bedside wishing to take his pulse; Zengyuan smiled and said: "I have prayed for death for twenty years past—would I now pray to live twenty years hence?
translations.idiomatic: When his illness turned critical, Huang Zongxi came to his bedside to feel his pulse. Zengyuan smiled and said, "I have prayed for death these twenty years past—would I now pray to live another twenty?

sentences.zh: 」宗羲泫然而別。

translations.literal: " Zongxi parted with tears streaming.
translations.idiomatic: " Zongxi took his leave with tears streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 同時有周齊曾者，字思沂，號唯一，鄞人，增遠同年進士也。

translations.literal: At the same time there was Zhou Qizeng, style name Siyi, sobriquet Weiyi, a native of Yin, a fellow jinshi graduate of Zengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time there was Zhou Qizeng, courtesy name Siyi, sobriquet Weiyi, a native of Yin and Zengyuan's fellow jinshi.

sentences.zh: 知廣東順德縣事，變社倉為義田，而以社倉之法行之。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Shunde County in Guangdong, converted the community granary into charity farmland, and administered it by the methods of the community granary.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Shunde County in Guangdong, he converted the community granary into charity fields and managed them by the old granary rules.

sentences.zh: 國變後，棄官遯入剡源，盡去其發為發塚，架險立飄榜，曰「囊雲」，自稱無發居士。

translations.literal: After the dynastic change he abandoned office and fled into Shanyuan, utterly removed his hair and made a mound of it, erected a perch in a perilous spot and set up a floating placard reading "Bag of Clouds," calling himself the Lay Buddhist Without Hair.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he abandoned his post and fled into Shanyuan, cut off all his hair and heaped it into a burial mound, built a perch on a perilous height and raised a floating placard inscribed "Encasing Clouds," and styled himself the Lay Buddhist Without Hair.

sentences.zh: 剡源饒水石，與山僧樵子出沒瀑聲虹影間。

translations.literal: Shanyuan abounded in water and rock; with mountain monks and woodcutters he appeared and disappeared amid waterfall sounds and rainbow reflections.
translations.idiomatic: Shanyuan abounded in streams and stone; with mountain monks and woodcutters he came and went amid the roar of waterfalls and the shimmer of rainbows.

sentences.zh: 天錫訪之，拒曰：「咫尺清輝，舉目有山河之異，不原見也。

translations.literal: Tianxi visited him; he refused, saying: "Within a foot's clear radiance, lifting the eyes one sees the rivers and mountains are changed—I do not wish to meet.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxi came to visit, he refused him, saying, "The clear moonlight is but a foot away, yet lifting my eyes I see rivers and mountains transformed—I do not wish to meet.

sentences.zh: 」為詩文，機鋒電激，汪洋自恣，寓言十九。

translations.literal: " In his poetry and prose his wit flashed like lightning, vast and self-indulgent, nine tenths allegory.
translations.idiomatic: " In his poetry and prose his wit struck like lightning; his style was vast and unrestrained, and nine parts in ten were allegory.

sentences.zh: 然清苦自立，胸中兀然有所不可，與增遠無二也。

translations.literal: Yet he stood on austere hardship, with something adamant in his breast that could not be bent—no different from Zengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lived in austere self-reliance, with something unyielding in his breast that would not bend—no different from Zengyuan.

sentences.zh: 黃宗羲嘗為兩人合志其墓雲。

translations.literal: Huang Zongxi once composed a joint epitaph for the tombs of the two men.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi once wrote a joint epitaph for the graves of the two men.

sentences.zh: 傅山，字青主，陽曲人。

translations.literal: Fu Shan, style name Qingzhu, a native of Yangqu.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Shan, courtesy name Qingzhu, was a native of Yangqu.

sentences.zh: 六歲，啖黃精，不穀食，強之，乃飯。

translations.literal: At six he ate yellow essence and did not eat grain; when forced, he then took rice.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of six he ate yellow essence and would not eat grain; only when pressed did he take rice.

sentences.zh: 讀書過目成誦。

translations.literal: In reading books he could recite them after one look.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he read he could recite after a single perusal.

sentences.zh: 明季天下將亂，諸號為搢紳先生者，多迂腐不足道，憤之，乃堅苦持氣節，不少媕冘。

translations.literal: In the late Ming the realm was about to fall into disorder; those styled gentry and masters were mostly pedantic and unworthy of mention; he resented this, and so steadfastly endured hardship and upheld integrity, not the least fawning or servile.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming, as the realm was sliding toward chaos, the so-called gentry and masters were for the most part pedantic and unworthy of respect. He resented this and steadfastly bore hardship to uphold his integrity, never yielding to flattery or servility.

sentences.zh: 提學袁繼咸為巡按張孫振所誣，孫振，閹黨也。

translations.literal: Education intendant Yuan Jixian was slandered by censor Zhang Sunzhen; Sunzhen was of the eunuch faction.
translations.idiomatic: Education intendant Yuan Jixian was framed by touring censor Zhang Sunzhen, who belonged to the eunuch faction.

sentences.zh: 山約同學曹良直等詣通政使，三上書訟之，巡撫吳甡亦直袁，遂得雪。

translations.literal: Shan joined classmates Cao Liangzhi and others in going to the Commissioner of Transmission, thrice submitting memorials on his behalf; Governor Wu Shen also upheld Yuan, and he was exonerated.
translations.idiomatic: Shan joined his classmate Cao Liangzhi and others in petitioning the Commissioner of Transmission, submitting three memorials in Yuan's defense; Governor Wu Shen also took Yuan's side, and the case was cleared.

sentences.zh: 山以此名聞一下，甲申後，山改黃冠裝，衣硃衣，居土穴，以養母。

translations.literal: Shan thereby became famed in the realm below; after the jiashen year Shan changed to Taoist dress, wore vermilion robes, dwelt in an earthen cave to nourish his mother.
translations.idiomatic: By this Shan's name spread throughout the land. After the jiashen year he adopted Taoist garb, wore vermilion robes, and lived in an earthen cave to support his mother.

sentences.zh: 繼咸自九江執歸燕邸，以難中詩遺山，且曰：「不敢媿友生也！

translations.literal: Jixian was taken prisoner from Jiujiang back to the Yan residence, sent Shan a poem composed amid hardship, and said: "I dare not shame my fellow students!
translations.idiomatic: Jixian was seized at Jiujiang and taken back to the Yan residence; he sent Shan a poem written in adversity, saying, "I dare not bring shame upon my fellow students!

sentences.zh: 」山省書，慟哭，曰：「嗚呼！

translations.literal: " Shan read the letter and wept bitterly, saying: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: " When Shan read the letter he wept bitterly and cried, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 吾亦安敢負公哉！

translations.literal: How could I dare fail you, sir!
translations.idiomatic: How could I dare fail you, sir!

sentences.zh: 順治十一年，以河南獄牽連被逮，抗詞不屈，絕粒九日，幾死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi, implicated in the Henan prison case he was arrested; his defiant words did not bend; he fasted nine days and nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Shunzhi he was implicated in the Henan prison affair and arrested; his defiant words did not yield, and he fasted for nine days, nearly dying.

sentences.zh: 門人中有以奇計救之，得免。

translations.literal: Among his disciples one used an ingenious plan to save him, and he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Among his disciples one devised a clever stratagem to save him, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 然山深自吒恨，謂不若速死為安，而其仰視天、俯視地者，未嘗一日止。

translations.literal: Yet Shan deeply regretted himself, saying that swift death would have been more at peace; yet his looking up to Heaven and looking down to Earth never ceased for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Shan bitterly reproached himself, saying that a swift death would have been peace; still, his looking up to Heaven and down to Earth never ceased for a single day.

sentences.zh: 比天下大定，始出與人接。

translations.literal: When the realm was largely settled, he began to go out and meet people.
translations.idiomatic: Only when the realm was largely pacified did he begin to go out and receive visitors.

sentences.zh: 康熙十七年，詔舉鴻博，給事中李宗孔薦，固辭。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi, an edict summoned men of broad learning; Vice Censor-in-chief Li Zongkong recommended him; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Kangxi an edict called for men of broad learning; Vice Censor-in-chief Li Zongkong recommended him, but he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 有司強迫，至令役夫舁其床以行。

translations.literal: The authorities forced him, even ordering laborers to carry his bed and go.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities pressed him relentlessly, even ordering laborers to carry his bed and set out.

sentences.zh: 至京師二十里，誓死不入。

translations.literal: Twenty li from the capital he vowed to die rather than enter.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li from the capital he swore he would die rather than enter the city.

sentences.zh: 大學士馮溥首過之，公卿畢至，山臥床不具迎送禮。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Feng Pu was first to visit him; all the lords and ministers arrived; Shan lay on his bed and did not perform the receiving and sending rites.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Feng Pu was the first to call on him; the high officials all came. Shan lay on his bed and offered no greeting or farewell ceremony.

sentences.zh: 魏象樞以老病上聞，詔免試，加內閣中書以寵之。

translations.literal: Wei Xiangshu reported his old illness to the throne; an edict excused him from the examination and added him as Secretariat drafter to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiangshu reported his age and illness to the throne; an edict excused him from the examination and appointed him Secretariat drafter as a mark of favor.

sentences.zh: 馮溥強其入謝，使人舁以入，望見大清門，淚涔涔下，僕於地。

translations.literal: Feng Pu forced him to enter to give thanks; men carried him in; when he saw the Great Qing Gate tears streamed down and he collapsed on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Pu pressed him to enter and give thanks; they carried him in. When he saw the Great Qing Gate his tears streamed down and he collapsed to the ground.

sentences.zh: 魏象樞進曰：「止，止，是即謝矣！

translations.literal: Wei Xiangshu stepped forward and said: "Stop, stop—that is thanks enough!
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiangshu stepped forward and said, "Enough, enough—that counts as your thanks!

sentences.zh: 」翼日歸，溥以下皆出城送之。

translations.literal: " The next day he returned; Feng and all below went out of the city to send him off.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day he set out for home; Feng Pu and all the officials below him went out of the city to see him off.

sentences.zh: 山歎曰：「今而後其脫然無累哉！

translations.literal: Shan sighed: "From now on may I be free of burdens!
translations.idiomatic: Shan sighed, "From now on I am finally free of encumbrance!

sentences.zh: 」既而曰：「使後世或妄以許衡、劉因輩賢我，且死不瞑目矣！

translations.literal: Then he said: "If later ages should rashly rank me with Xu Heng and Liu Yin, I would not close my eyes in death!
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "If later generations should rashly praise me alongside Xu Heng and Liu Yin, I would not close my eyes even in death!

sentences.zh: 」聞者咋舌。

translations.literal: " Those who heard this gasped.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who heard him gasped in shock.

sentences.zh: 至家，大吏咸造廬請謁。

translations.literal: On reaching home, great officials all came to his hut to request audience.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached home, high officials all came to his dwelling to pay their respects.

sentences.zh: 山冬夏著一布衣，自稱曰「民」。

translations.literal: Winter and summer Shan wore one cloth garment and called himself "a commoner."
translations.idiomatic: Winter and summer he wore a single cloth garment and called himself "a commoner."

sentences.zh: 或曰：「君非舍人乎？

translations.literal: Someone said: "Are you not a Secretariat drafter?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Are you not a Secretariat drafter?

sentences.zh: 」不應也。

translations.literal: " He did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: " He made no reply.

sentences.zh: 卒，以硃衣、黃冠斂。

translations.literal: At death he was enshrouded in vermilion robes and a yellow Daoist cap.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was laid out in vermilion robes and a yellow Daoist cap.

sentences.zh: 山工書畫，謂：「書寧拙毋巧，寧醜毋媚，寧支離毋輕滑，寧真率毋安排。

translations.literal: Shan was skilled in calligraphy and painting, saying: "In writing, better clumsy than clever, better ugly than flattering, better fragmented than slick and light, better sincere and direct than contrived.
translations.idiomatic: Shan excelled at calligraphy and painting. He said, "In writing, better clumsy than clever, better ugly than flattering, better fragmented than slick and facile, better sincere and direct than contrived.

sentences.zh: 」人謂此言非止言書也。

translations.literal: " People said these words were not only about writing.
translations.idiomatic: " People said these words were not merely about calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 詩文初學韓昌黎，崛強自喜，後信筆抒寫，俳調俗語，皆入筆端，不原以此名家矣。

translations.literal: In poetry and prose he at first studied Han Yu, proud and self-satisfied; later he wrote freely as the brush moved, banter and common speech all entered his page—he did not wish to be famed for this.
translations.idiomatic: In poetry and prose he first studied Han Yu and wrote with stubborn pride; later he let the brush run freely, and banter and colloquial speech all found their way onto the page—though he did not wish to be known for that.

sentences.zh: 著有霜紅龕集十二卷。

translations.literal: He authored the Collected Works from the Frost-Red Shrine in twelve juan.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Collected Works from the Frost-Red Shrine in twelve juan.

sentences.zh: 子眉，先卒，詩亦附焉。

translations.literal: His son Mei died before him; Mei's poems were also appended.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mei died before him; Mei's poems were appended as well.

sentences.zh: 眉，字壽髦。

translations.literal: Mei, style name Shoumao.
translations.idiomatic: Mei, courtesy name Shoumao.

sentences.zh: 每日出樵，置書擔上，休則把讀。

translations.literal: Each day he went out to gather firewood, set books on his carrying pole, and when resting took them up to read.
translations.idiomatic: Each day he went out to cut firewood, laid his books on the carrying pole, and when he rested took them up to read.

sentences.zh: 山常賣藥四方，與眉共挽一車，暮抵逆旅，篝燈課經，力學，繼父志。

translations.literal: Shan often sold medicine in all directions; with Mei they together pulled one cart; at evening they reached an inn, lit a lamp to study the classics, exerting learning, continuing his father's will.
translations.idiomatic: Shan often traveled selling medicine; he and Mei together pulled a single cart. In the evening they would reach an inn, light a lamp, and study the classics, striving in learning to carry on his father's purpose.

sentences.zh: 與客談中州文獻，滔滔不盡。

translations.literal: With guests he discussed Central Plains literature—talked without end.
translations.idiomatic: When speaking with guests of the literary heritage of the Central Plains, his words flowed on without end.

sentences.zh: 山喜苦酒，自稱老糱禪，眉乃稱小糱禪。

translations.literal: Shan delighted in bitter wine, called himself Old Leaven Chan; Mei then called himself Little Leaven Chan.
translations.idiomatic: Shan loved strong wine and called himself Old Leaven Chan; Mei in turn called himself Little Leaven Chan.

sentences.zh: 費密，字此度，新繁人。

translations.literal: Fei Mi, style name Cidu, a native of Xinfan.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Mi, courtesy name Cidu, was a native of Xinfan.

sentences.zh: 父經虞，明雲南昆明縣知縣。

translations.literal: His father Jingyu was magistrate of Kunming County in Yunnan under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingyu had been magistrate of Kunming County in Yunnan under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 密年十四，父病，醫言嘗糞甘苦，可知生死，密嘗而苦，父病果起。

translations.literal: When Mi was fourteen his father fell ill; the physician said tasting the stool's sweet or bitter could show life or death; Mi tasted it and it was bitter; his father's illness indeed recovered.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was fourteen his father fell ill. The physician said that if the stool tasted sweet or bitter one could know life or death. Mi tasted it and found it bitter; his father's illness then recovered.

sentences.zh: 未幾，流賊張獻忠犯蜀，密上書巡按御史劉之勃，陳戰守策，不省。

translations.literal: Before long the bandit Zhang Xianzhong invaded Shu; Mi submitted a memorial to censor Liu Zhibo setting forth strategies of war and defense—it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebel Zhang Xianzhong invaded Shu. Mi submitted a memorial to touring censor Liu Zhibo outlining strategies of defense and attack, but it went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 已而全蜀皆陷，密展轉窮山中，會有人傳其父滇中消息，聞之痛哭，遂去家入滇。

translations.literal: Soon all Shu fell; Mi wandered in turn through remote mountains; by chance someone brought news of his father from Yunnan; hearing it he wept bitterly and left home to enter Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon all of Shu fell. Mi wandered from one remote mountain to another until someone brought word of his father in Yunnan. On hearing it he wept bitterly and left home for Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 經歷蠻峒中，奉父自滇歸蜀。

translations.literal: Passing through barbarian ravines, he brought his father from Yunnan back to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through barbarian ravines, he escorted his father from Yunnan back to Shu.

sentences.zh: 至建昌衛，為凹者蠻所得，父賂蠻人，始脫歸。

translations.literal: Reaching Jianchang Guard, they were taken by the Wa barbarians; the father bribed the barbarians before they escaped home.
translations.idiomatic: At Jianchang Guard they were seized by Wa tribesmen; only after his father bribed the barbarians did they escape and return home.

sentences.zh: 明將楊展聞密名，遣使致聘，密乃說展曰：「賊亂數年，民且無食，今非屯田，無以救蜀民，且兵不能自立。

translations.literal: Ming general Yang Zhan hearing Mi's name sent envoys to invite him; Mi then urged Zhan: "The bandits have ravaged for years; the people are nearly without food; now without military colonies there is no way to save the people of Shu, and moreover the army cannot stand on its own.
translations.idiomatic: Ming general Yang Zhan, hearing of Mi's reputation, sent envoys to invite him. Mi then urged Zhan, "The rebels have ravaged for years and the people are nearly starving. Without military colonies there is no way to save the people of Shu, and the army itself cannot sustain itself.

sentences.zh: 」展納其言，命子總兵官璟偕密屯田於榮經瓦屋山之楊村，以次舉其法，行諸州縣。

translations.literal: " Zhan accepted his words, ordered his son the regional commander Jing to join Mi in military colonies at Yang Village on Mount Wagwu in Rongjing, and in succession extended the method, implementing it in all prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhan accepted his advice and ordered his son, regional commander Jing, to join Mi in opening military colonies at Yang Village on Mount Wagwu in Rongjing. The method was then extended step by step and carried out in prefectures and counties throughout the region.

sentences.zh: 後展為袁韜、武大定所殺，密與璟整師為復仇計，嘗與賊戰，躬自擐甲，左手為刃所傷。

translations.literal: Later Zhan was killed by Yuan Tao and Wu Dading; Mi and Jing marshaled troops to plan revenge; they often fought the bandits; Mi personally donned armor, his left hand wounded by a blade.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhan was killed by Yuan Tao and Wu Dading. Mi and Jing gathered troops to plan revenge; they often fought the rebels, and Mi personally donned armor, his left hand cut by a blade.

sentences.zh: 時璟營於峨眉，裨將有與花溪民毆爭者，言「花溪居民下石擊吾營，勢且反」以怒璟。

translations.literal: At that time Jing encamped at Emei; a lieutenant had a brawl with Huaxi townspeople, saying "The Huaxi residents are pelting our camp with stones and are about to rebel," to enrage Jing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jing was encamped at Emei. A lieutenant brawled with townspeople of Huaxi and reported that the Huaxi residents were pelting the camp with stones and were on the verge of revolt, inflaming Jing's anger.

sentences.zh: 璟欲引兵誅之，密力爭曰：「花溪，吾民也。

translations.literal: Jing wished to lead troops to punish them; Mi strove against it: "Huaxi—that is our people.
translations.idiomatic: Jing wished to lead troops to punish them. Mi argued forcefully, "Huaxi is our own people.

sentences.zh: 方與賊戰而殺吾民，彼變從賊，是益賊也。

translations.literal: While fighting the bandits you kill our people—they will turn and follow the bandits; that only adds to the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: If while fighting the rebels you kill our own people, they will turn and join the rebels—that only strengthens the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」璟乃止，全活數百家。

translations.literal: " Jing then stopped, and several hundred households were wholly saved.
translations.idiomatic: " Jing then desisted, and several hundred households were spared.

sentences.zh: 後密還成都省墓，至新津，為武大定兵所掠。

translations.literal: Later Mi returned to Chengdu to visit his parents' tombs; reaching Xinjin he was seized by Wu Dading's soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mi returned to Chengdu to tend his parents' graves; at Xinjin he was seized by Wu Dading's troops.

sentences.zh: 知密嘗參展軍事，欲殺之，以計得免。

translations.literal: Knowing Mi had once taken part in Zhan's military affairs, they wished to kill him; by a stratagem he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Mi had once served in Zhan's army, they meant to kill him, but by a ruse he escaped.

sentences.zh: 密歎曰：「既不能報國，又不能庇親及身，不如舍而他去！

translations.literal: Mi sighed: "Having neither been able to serve the state, nor able to protect kin and body, better to leave them and go elsewhere!
translations.idiomatic: Mi sighed, "Unable to serve the state, unable to shelter kin or even myself—better to leave all this and go elsewhere!

sentences.zh: 」遂奉父由成都北行入秦，溯漢江，下吳、越，流寓泰州，老焉。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led his father north from Chengdu into Qin, went up the Han River, descended to Wu and Yue, sojourned at Taizhou, and grew old there.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon he led his father north from Chengdu into Qin, traveled up the Han River, went down through Wu and Yue, and settled at Taizhou, where he lived out his years.

sentences.zh: 經虞邃於經學，嘗著毛詩廣義、雅論諸書，以漢儒註說為宗。

translations.literal: Jingyu was profound in classical learning, and had written such works as Extended Meaning of the Mao Odes and Treatises on Elegance, taking Han Ru commentaries as orthodox.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu was deeply learned in the classics and had written works such as Extended Meaning of the Mao Odes and Treatises on Elegance, taking Han Confucian commentaries as his standard.

sentences.zh: 密盡傳父業，又博證學士大夫，與王復禮、毛甡、閻若璩交，密一足跛，後往蘇門謁孫奇逢，稱弟子。

translations.literal: Mi fully transmitted his father's learning, also broadly verified among scholars and gentlemen; he associated with Wang Fuli, Mao Qi, and Yan Ruoqu; Mi was lame in one foot; later he went to Sumen to visit Sun Qifeng and styled himself his disciple.
translations.idiomatic: Mi fully inherited his father's scholarship and also sought wide verification among learned gentlemen. He associated with Wang Fuli, Mao Qi, and Yan Ruoqu. Lame in one foot, he later went to Sumen to visit Sun Qifeng and styled himself his disciple.

sentences.zh: 工詩、古文，俯仰取給於授徒、賣文，人咸重其品，悲其遇。

translations.literal: Skilled in poetry and ancient prose, he made his living up and down from teaching pupils and selling writings; people all esteemed his character and pitied his fate.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in poetry and ancient prose, he supported himself by teaching and selling his writings; all who knew him respected his integrity and grieved his hard lot.

sentences.zh: 州守為之除徭役，杜門三十年，著書甚多。

translations.literal: The prefect exempted him from corvée labor; for thirty years he shut his door and wrote many books.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect exempted him from corvée service; for thirty years he shut his door and wrote extensively.

sentences.zh: 密謂宋人以周、程接孔、孟，盡黜二千餘年儒者為未聞道，乃上稽古經、正史，旁及群書，作中傳正紀百二十卷，序儒者授受源流，自子夏始。

translations.literal: Mi held that Song people connected Zhou and Cheng to Confucius and Mencius, entirely dismissing more than two thousand years of Ru as never having heard the Way; he therefore traced upward the ancient classics and standard histories, and ranged widely through collected books, composing Correct Annals of the Central Tradition in 120 juan, narrating the succession and transmission of Ru from Zixia onward.
translations.idiomatic: Mi held that Song scholars, linking Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers to Confucius and Mencius, dismissed more than two thousand years of Confucians as never having grasped the Way. He therefore traced the ancient classics and standard histories upward and ranged widely through other books, composing the Correct Annals of the Central Tradition in 120 juan to narrate the line of transmission among Confucians from Zixia onward.

sentences.zh: 又作弘道書十卷、古今篤論四卷、中旨定錄四卷、中旨辨錄四卷、中旨申感四卷，皆申明弘道書之旨。

translations.literal: He also wrote Expounding the Way in 10 juan, Earnest Discourses Ancient and Modern in 4 juan, Fixed Records of the Central Purport in 4 juan, Discriminating Records of the Central Purport in 4 juan, and Expressing Resonance of the Central Purport in 4 juan—all expounding the purport of Expounding the Way.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Expounding the Way in ten juan, Earnest Discourses Ancient and Modern in four juan, Fixed Records of the Central Purport in four juan, Discriminating Records of the Central Purport in four juan, and Expressing Resonance of the Central Purport in four juan—all clarifying the aims of Expounding the Way.

sentences.zh: 又有尚書說、周官注論、二南偶說、中庸大學駮議、四禮補篇、史記箋、古史正、歷代貢舉合議、費氏家訓及詩文集。

translations.literal: There were also Commentary on the Documents, Commentary Discussions on the Offices of Zhou, Occasional Remarks on the Two Nan, Refutations of the Doctrine of the Mean and Great Learning, Supplements to the Four Rites, Commentary on the Records of the Grand Historian, Corrections to Ancient History, Combined Discussions on Tribute and Selection Through the Ages, Instructions for the Fei Family, and collected poetry and prose.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Commentary on the Documents, Commentary Discussions on the Offices of Zhou, Occasional Remarks on the Two Nan, Refutations of the Doctrine of the Mean and Great Learning, Supplements to the Four Rites, Commentary on the Records of the Grand Historian, Corrections to Ancient History, Combined Discussions on Tribute and Selection Through the Ages, Instructions for the Fei Family, and collected poetry and prose.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 子錫琮、錫璜，世其學。

translations.literal: His sons Xicong and Xihuang inherited his learning.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Xicong and Xihuang carried on his scholarship.

sentences.zh: 王弘撰，字無異，號山史，華陰人。

translations.literal: Wang Hongzhuan, style name Wuyi, sobriquet Shanshi, a native of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongzhuan, courtesy name Wuyi, sobriquet Shanshi, was a native of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 明諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a licentiate under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 博雅能古文，嗜金石，藏古書畫金石最富。

translations.literal: Broadly learned and able in ancient prose, addicted to metal and stone—inscriptions; he collected ancient books, paintings, and metal and stone most richly.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and skilled in ancient prose, he was devoted to epigraphy and possessed the richest collection of ancient books, paintings, and bronze and stone inscriptions.

sentences.zh: 又通濂、洛、關、閩之學，好易，精圖像。

translations.literal: He also mastered the learning of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min, loved the Changes, and was expert in diagrams and images.
translations.idiomatic: He also mastered the traditions associated with Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, Zhang Zai, and the Fujian school, loved the Book of Changes, and was expert in cosmological diagrams.

sentences.zh: 學者翕然宗之，關中入士領袖也。

translations.literal: Scholars all revered him as their standard; he was the leader of scholars who entered within the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars revered him as their leader; he stood at the head of learning in the Guanzhong region.

sentences.zh: 與李顒、李柏、李因篤齊名，時以得一言為榮。

translations.literal: His fame rivaled Li Yong, Li Bai, and Li Yindu; at the time to receive one word from him was counted glory.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation stood with Li Yong, Li Bai, and Li Yindu; in those days to receive a single remark from him was counted an honor.

sentences.zh: 凡碑版銘志非三李則弘撰，而弘撰工書法，故求者多於三李。

translations.literal: All stele inscriptions and epitaphs were entrusted to the Three Lis or Hongzhuan; and Hongzhuan was skilled in calligraphy, so requests came to him more than to the Three Lis.
translations.idiomatic: Epitaphs and commemorative inscriptions went to the Three Lis or to Hongzhuan; because Hongzhuan excelled at calligraphy, commissions came to him even more than to the Three Lis.

sentences.zh: 弘撰交遊遍天下，甲申後，奔走結納，尤著志節。

translations.literal: Hongzhuan's acquaintances ranged through all the realm; after jiashen he rushed about forming connections, especially renowned for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhuan's acquaintances spanned the realm; after the jiashen year he traveled widely forging ties, and was especially noted for his steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 顧炎武遍觀四方，至華陰，謂秦人慕經學、重處士、持清議，他邦所少；

translations.literal: Gu Yanwu viewed all four quarters; reaching Huayin he said the people of Qin admire classical learning, esteem recluses, and hold to pure criticism—things few in other regions share;
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanwu had traveled throughout the realm; when he came to Huayin he said that the people of Qin admire classical learning, esteem recluses, and uphold pure criticism—qualities rare in other regions;

sentences.zh: 華陰綰轂之口，雖足不出戶，而能見天下之人，聞天下之事。

translations.literal: Huayin was a hub where roads converged; though he did not step outside his door, he could see all the people under heaven and hear all affairs under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: and that Huayin lay where the roads met, so that though one never left his door he could still meet men from all the realm and hear news of all the world.

sentences.zh: 欲定居，弘撰為營齋舍居之。

translations.literal: Wishing to settle, Hongzhuan built a study lodge for him to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu wished to settle there, Hongzhuan had a study lodge built for him to live in.

sentences.zh: 炎武嘗曰：「好學不倦，篤於朋友，吾不如王山史。

translations.literal: Yanwu once said: "Love of learning without weariness, devotion to friends—I am not the equal of Wang Shanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Gu once said, "In tireless love of learning and devotion to friends, I am not the equal of Wang Shanshi.

sentences.zh: 」當時儒碩遺逸皆與弘撰往還，頗推重之。

translations.literal: " At the time eminent Confucians and recluses all associated with Hongzhuan and greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Men of learning and recluses throughout the land all associated with Hongzhuan and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 弘撰嘗集炎武及孫枝蔚、閻爾梅等數十人所與書札，合為一冊，手題曰友聲集，各​​注姓氏。

translations.literal: Hongzhuan once gathered letters exchanged with Yanwu and several dozen others including Sun Zhiwei and Yan Ermei, combined them into one fascicle, inscribed it by hand as Collection of Friendly Voices, and beside each name noted the surname.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhuan once gathered the letters he had exchanged with Gu Yanwu and several dozen others, including Sun Zhiwei and Yan Ermei, bound them into a single volume, inscribed it by hand as Collection of Friendly Voices, and annotated each entry with the writer's surname.

sentences.zh: 中有為謀炎武卜居華下事，言：「此舉大有關係，世道人心，實皆攸賴，唯速圖之！

translations.literal: Among them was planning for Yanwu to divine a dwelling below Mount Hua, saying: "This matter is greatly consequential; the temper of the age and men's hearts truly all depend on it—only hasten to plan it!
translations.idiomatic: One letter concerned plans to establish Gu below Mount Hua, declaring, "This step matters profoundly—the age and the hearts of men truly depend on it; act quickly!

sentences.zh: 」蓋當日華下集議，實有所為也。

translations.literal: " For the gatherings below Hua in those days truly had their purpose.
translations.idiomatic: " The gatherings held below Mount Hua in those days, in short, truly had their aims.

sentences.zh: 康熙間，以鴻博徵，不赴。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era he was summoned through the Boxue examination and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kangxi reign he was summoned through the special Boxue examination but declined to attend.

sentences.zh: 初與因篤同學，甚密，及因篤就徵，遂與之絕。

translations.literal: Initially he studied with Yindu and were very close; when Yindu answered the summons, he broke with him.
translations.idiomatic: He had studied closely with Li Yindu, but when Li accepted the imperial summons, Hongzhuan broke off the friendship.

sentences.zh: 弘撰所居華山下，有讀易廬，與華峰相向，稱絕勝。

translations.literal: Where Hongzhuan dwelt below Mount Hua was the Lodge for Reading the Changes, facing Mount Hua's peak—called unsurpassed beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Below Mount Hua, where Hongzhuan lived, stood the Lodge for Reading the Changes, facing the central peak—a scene acclaimed as unrivaled.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十有五。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 著有易像圖說、山志、砥齋集。

translations.literal: His works include Illustrations of Yi Imagery, Mountain Gazetteer, and Dizhai Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Illustrations of Yi Imagery, a mountain gazetteer, and the Dizhai Collection.

sentences.zh: 杜濬，字於皇，號茶村，黃岡人。

translations.literal: Du Jun, style name Yuhuang, sobriquet Chacun, a native of Huanggang.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jun, courtesy name Yuhuang, sobriquet Chacun, was a native of Huanggang.

sentences.zh: 明季為諸生，避亂居金陵。

translations.literal: At the end of the Ming he was a licentiate; fleeing turmoil he lived in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Ming he was a licentiate; fleeing the turmoil, he settled in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 少倜儻，嘗欲著奇節，既不得試，遂刻意為詩，然不欲以詩人自名也。

translations.literal: In youth unrestrained, he once wished to achieve singular distinction; denied the chance to prove himself, he turned to poetry with deliberate effort, yet did not wish to be known as a poet.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and unconventional and once aspired to singular deeds of honor; denied the chance to prove himself, he devoted himself to poetry, yet refused to be known merely as a poet.

sentences.zh: 於並世人獨重宣城沈壽民、吳中徐枋，自媿不如。

translations.literal: Among contemporaries he uniquely esteemed Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng and Xu Fang of Wu, and felt himself their inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Among his contemporaries he uniquely esteemed Shen Shoumin of Xuancheng and Xu Fang of Wu, and considered himself their inferior.

sentences.zh: 其在金陵，與方仲舒善，仲舒，苞父也。

translations.literal: In Jinling he was close to Fang Zhongshu—Zhongshu was Bao's father.
translations.idiomatic: In Jinling he was close to Fang Zhongshu, who was Fang Bao's father.

sentences.zh: 金陵冠蓋輻輳，諸公貴人求詩者踵至，多謝絕。

translations.literal: Jinling teemed with officials; nobles seeking poems came in succession—he mostly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Jinling swarmed with officials and notables; those who came seeking poems arrived in an unbroken stream, and he mostly turned them away.

sentences.zh: 錢謙益嘗造訪，至閉門不與通，惟故舊徒步到門，則偶接焉。

translations.literal: Qian Qianyi once called on him; Jun shut the door and would not admit him—only old friends who came on foot might occasionally be received.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qianyi once called on him, but Jun shut the door and would not receive him; only old friends who came on foot might occasionally be admitted.

sentences.zh: 門內為竹關，關外設坐，約客至，視鍵閉，則坐而待，不得叩關，雖大府至，亦然。

translations.literal: Inside the gate was a bamboo barrier; outside it a seat was placed. It was agreed that when a guest came, if the lock was shut he should sit and wait and must not knock—even grandees were treated the same.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the gate stood a bamboo barrier, with a seat placed outside. Guests were told that if the lock was closed they must sit and wait and must not knock on the gate—even high officials were subject to the same rule.

sentences.zh: 及功令有挑門之役，有司按籍欲優免，濬曰：「是吾所服也！

translations.literal: When regulations required night-watch door duty, officials checking registers wished to exempt him preferentially; Jun said: "That is what I ought to serve!
translations.idiomatic: When regulations imposed night-watch duty at the gates, officials reviewing the registers sought to exempt him; Jun said, "That is a duty I ought to perform!

sentences.zh: 」躬雜廝輿夜巡綽，眾莫能止。

translations.literal: " Personally he mingled with runners and sedan bearers on night patrol, and none could stop him.
translations.idiomatic: " He himself joined the runners and chair bearers on night patrol, and none could dissuade him.

sentences.zh: 嗜茗飲，嘗言吾有絕糧，無絕茶。

translations.literal: He loved tea, and used to say, "I may run out of grain, but never out of tea."
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to tea and used to say, "I may run out of grain, but never out of tea."

sentences.zh: 既有花塚，因拾殘茗聚封之，謂之「茶丘」。

translations.literal: Having a Flower Mound, he gathered spent tea leaves and sealed them in heaps, calling them "Tea Hills."
translations.idiomatic: He had a Flower Mound, and would gather spent tea leaves and seal them into mounds he called "Tea Hills."

sentences.zh: 年七十七，卒於揚州。

translations.literal: He died at seventy-seven in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-seven in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 喪歸，故人謀卜兆，子世濟曰：「吾有親，而以葬事辱二三君乎？

translations.literal: When the coffin returned, old friends planned to choose a grave site; his son Shiji said: "I have parents living—shall I impose the burial on you gentlemen?
translations.idiomatic: When the coffin was brought home, old friends planned to choose a burial site, but his son Shiji said, "I still have parents living—how could I burden you gentlemen with the burial?

sentences.zh: 是謂我非人也。

translations.literal: That would mean I am not human.
translations.idiomatic: That would mean I am not human.

sentences.zh: 」亡何，世濟卒。

translations.literal: " Before long Shiji died.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long Shiji died as well.

sentences.zh: 又數年，陳鵬年來守金陵，始葬諸蔣山北梅花村。

translations.literal: Years later Chen Pengnian came as prefect of Jinling and only then buried him north of Mount Zhongshan at Plum Blossom Village.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later Chen Pengnian came as prefect of Jinling and at last buried him north of Mount Zhongshan at Plum Blossom Village.

sentences.zh: 濬詩最富，世所傳不及十一，手定者四十七冊。

translations.literal: Jun's poems were most abundant; less than a tenth circulated; what he revised himself filled forty-seven fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's poetry was exceedingly abundant; less than a tenth of it circulated in his lifetime, and what he revised by hand filled forty-seven fascicles.

sentences.zh: 吳偉業嘗云：「吾五言律得茶村焦山詩而始進。

translations.literal: Wu Weiye once said: "My regulated verse in five characters advanced only after Chacun's Jiaoshan poems."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Weiye once said, "My five-character regulated verse advanced only after I read Chacun's poems on Jiaoshan."

sentences.zh: 」閻若璩於時賢多所訾謷，獨許濬五律，稱為「詩聖」。

translations.literal: " Yan Ruoqu disparaged many talented men of the time but alone approved Jun's five-character regulated verse, calling him "sage of poetry."
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Ruoqu disparaged many talented men of the age, yet he alone approved Jun's five-character regulated verse and called him the "sage of poetry."

sentences.zh: 已刻者曰變雅堂集。

translations.literal: What was printed was titled Bianya Hall Collection.
translations.idiomatic: The work that was printed bears the title Bianya Hall Collection.

sentences.zh: 弟岕，字蒼略，號些山。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jie, style name Canglüe, sobriquet Xieshan.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Jie, courtesy name Canglüe, sobriquet Xieshan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 與兄同避亂金陵。

translations.literal: He fled turmoil to Jinling with his elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He fled the turmoil to Jinling together with his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 昆弟行身略同，而趣各異。

translations.literal: The brothers' conduct was broadly alike, yet their temperaments differed.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers' conduct was broadly similar, yet their temperaments differed.

sentences.zh: 濬峻廉隅，孤特自遂。

translations.literal: Jun was stern in integrity and solitary in following his own course.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was stern in integrity and solitary in following his own path.

sentences.zh: 遇名貴人，必以氣折之，於眾人未嘗接語言，用此叢忌嫉。

translations.literal: Meeting the famous and noble he always subdued them with spirit; toward the multitude he never exchanged words—thus he drew much envy.
translations.idiomatic: When he met the famous and powerful he always humbled them with his bearing; toward ordinary people he scarcely spoke at all, and for this he drew much resentment.

sentences.zh: 然名在天下，詩每出，遠近爭傳誦之。

translations.literal: Yet his name was under heaven; whenever a poem appeared, near and far competed to recite it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his fame spread throughout the realm, and whenever a new poem appeared, people near and far competed to recite it.

sentences.zh: 岕則退然自同於眾，所著詩歌、古文，雖子弟弗示也。

translations.literal: Jie by contrast withdrew and made himself one with the crowd; poems and ancient prose he wrote, he would not show even to his children.
translations.idiomatic: Jie, by contrast, withdrew and made himself one with the common people; the poetry and prose he wrote he would not show even to his own children.

sentences.zh: 方壯喪偶，不復娶。

translations.literal: While still in his prime he lost his wife and never remarried.
translations.idiomatic: While still in his prime he lost his wife and never remarried.

sentences.zh: 所居室漏且穿，木榻敝帷，數十年未嘗易。

translations.literal: His dwelling leaked and was pierced; wooden couch and tattered curtains—for decades he never changed them.
translations.idiomatic: His dwelling leaked and its roof was broken through; his wooden couch and tattered curtains he did not replace for decades.

sentences.zh: 室中終歲不掃除，每日中不得食，兒女啼號，客至無酒漿，意色間無幾微不自適者。

translations.literal: He never swept his room all year; often at midday he had no food; children wept; when guests came there was no wine—yet in his bearing there was scarcely a trace of discomfort.
translations.idiomatic: He never swept his room all year long; often at midday he had nothing to eat, his children wailed, and when guests came there was no wine—yet in his expression there was scarcely a trace of discontent.

sentences.zh: 行於途，常避人，不中道與人言，雖兒童廝輿，惟恐或傷之也。

translations.literal: Walking on the road he always avoided people, never spoke mid-path; even with children or runners he feared he might hurt them.
translations.idiomatic: On the road he always gave way to others and never stopped mid-path to speak; even with children or servants he feared he might somehow harm them.

sentences.zh: 後兄七年卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: He died seven years after his brother, at seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died seven years after his brother, at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 有些山集。

translations.literal: There is the Xieshan Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works are titled the Xieshan Collection.

sentences.zh: 郭都賢，字天門，益陽人。

translations.literal: Guo Duxian, style name Tianmen, a native of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Duxian, courtesy name Tianmen, was a native of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 天啟壬戌進士，授行人。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the Renxu year of Tianqi; appointed Bearer of Messages.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the renxu year of the Tianqi reign and was appointed Bearer of Messages.

sentences.zh: 分校順天鄉試，得史可法等六人。

translations.literal: Grading the Shuntian provincial examination, he selected six men including Shi Kefa.
translations.idiomatic: While grading the Shuntian provincial examination, he selected six candidates including Shi Kefa.

sentences.zh: 歷官員外郎，出為四川參議，督江​​西學政，分守嶺北道，巡撫江西。

translations.literal: He rose to Vice Director, went out as Sichuan Assistant Commissioner, supervised Jiangxi education, held the Lingbei circuit, and served as Governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director, was posted as assistant commissioner of Sichuan, supervised education in Jiangxi, held the Lingbei circuit, and served as governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時張獻忠已逼境，賊騎充斥。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Xianzhong had already pressed the borders; rebel horsemen filled the land.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Xianzhong had already pressed upon the borders, and rebel horsemen filled the countryside.

sentences.zh: 都賢晝夜繕守禦，兵餉無措，乃大會屬僚，凡官司一應供給，皆捐以助餉。

translations.literal: Duxian day and night repaired defenses; military funds had no source; he therefore convened subordinates and all official perquisites and supplies were donated to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: Duxian repaired the defenses day and night; with no funds for the troops, he convened his subordinates and had every official allowance and supply donated to the war effort.

sentences.zh: 左良玉屯兵九江，驕蹇觀望，都賢惡其淫掠，檄歸之，而募士兵為戍。

translations.literal: Zuo Liangyu camped at Jiujiang, proud and watching; Duxian detested his pillaging, ordered him back by proclamation, and recruited local troops for garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Liangyu encamped at Jiujiang, arrogant and holding back; Duxian detested his looting, recalled him by official dispatch, and recruited local militia to hold the defenses.

sentences.zh: 會有尼之者，遂乞病，棄官入廬山。

translations.literal: When someone obstructed him, he begged illness, abandoned office, and entered Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When opponents blocked his efforts, he pleaded illness, resigned his post, and withdrew to Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 逾年，北京陷，悲憤不食。

translations.literal: A year later Beijing fell; grief-stricken he refused food.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Beijing fell; stricken with grief, he refused to eat.

sentences.zh: 南都建號，史可法開閫揚州，薦授以官，辭不赴。

translations.literal: The Southern Capital established its reign; Shi Kefa opened command at Yangzhou and recommended him for office—he declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Capital established its regime, Shi Kefa opened command at Yangzhou and recommended him for office, but he declined and did not go.

sentences.zh: 桂王立肇慶，以兵部尚書召，而都賢已祝髮為僧矣。

translations.literal: Prince Gui was set up at Zhaoqing and summoned him as Minister of War—but Duxian had already shaved his head and become a monk.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Gui was enthroned at Zhaoqing, he was summoned as Minister of War, but Duxian had already shaved his head and become a monk.

sentences.zh: 先是洪承疇坐事落職，都賢奏請起用，至是承疇經略西南，以故舊謁都賢於山中，餽以金，不受；

translations.literal: Earlier Hong Chengchou was dismissed for an offense and Duxian memorialized to restore him; now Chengchou was grand coordinator of the southwest and visited Duxian in the mountains as an old acquaintance, offering gold—he would not accept;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Hong Chengchou was dismissed for an offense, Duxian had memorialized for his reinstatement; now Chengchou was grand coordinator of the southwest and visited Duxian in the mountains as an old friend, offering gold, which Duxian refused;

sentences.zh: 奏攜其子監軍，亦堅辭。

translations.literal: He memorialized to bring his son to supervise the army—Duxian also firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Chengchou also petitioned to have his son accompany the army as supervisor, but Duxian firmly refused that as well.

sentences.zh: 都賢見承疇時，故作目瞇狀，承疇驚問何時得目疾，都賢曰：「始吾識公時，目故有疾。

translations.literal: When Duxian met Chengchou he deliberately feigned squinting eyes; Chengchou asked in alarm when he had gotten eye disease; Duxian said: "When I first knew you, your eyes already had the ailment.
translations.idiomatic: When Duxian met Chengchou he deliberately feigned a squint; Chengchou asked in alarm when he had developed eye trouble; Duxian said, "When I first knew you, your eyes already had the ailment.

sentences.zh: 」承疇默然。

translations.literal: " Chengchou was silent.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengchou fell silent.

sentences.zh: 都賢篤至性，哀樂過人，嚴而介，風骨嶄然。

translations.literal: Duxian was deeply true in nature; joy and grief exceeded other men; stern and upright, his bearing stood sharply forth.
translations.idiomatic: Duxian was profoundly sincere by nature; his joy and grief exceeded those of ordinary men; stern and upright, his bearing stood out sharply.

sentences.zh: 博學強識，工詩文，書法瘦硬，兼善繪事，寫竹尤入妙。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with strong memory, skilled in poetry and prose; calligraphy lean and hard; also good at painting, bamboo especially entering sublimity.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned with a formidable memory, he was skilled in poetry and prose; his calligraphy was lean and forceful; he was also accomplished at painting, and his bamboo paintings especially reached mastery.

sentences.zh: 僧號頑石，又號些菴。

translations.literal: His monk name was Wanshi, also called Xie'an.
translations.idiomatic: As a monk he took the name Wanshi and also styled himself Xie'an.

sentences.zh: 茹苦，無定居。

translations.literal: He endured bitterness and had no fixed abode.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in hardship and had no fixed dwelling.

sentences.zh: 初依熊開元、尹民興於嘉魚，住梅熟菴；

translations.literal: Initially he relied on Xiong Kaiyuan and Yin Minxing at Jiayu, lodging at the Meishu Hermitage;
translations.idiomatic: At first he stayed with Xiong Kaiyuan and Yin Minxing at Jiayu, residing at the Meishu Hermitage;

sentences.zh: 已，流寓海陽，築補山堂：前後十九年。

translations.literal: Later he sojourned at Haiyang and built the Bushan Hall—for nineteen years in all.
translations.idiomatic: later he sojourned at Haiyang and built the Bushan Hall, where he remained for nineteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 歸結草廬桃花江。

translations.literal: Returning he built a thatched hut on Peach Blossom River.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually returned and built a thatched hut on Peach Blossom River.

sentences.zh: 客死江寧承天寺。

translations.literal: He died as a guest at Chengtian Temple in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: He died away from home at Chengtian Temple in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 有女名純貞，許字黔國公沐氏，變後，音問梗絕，遂終於家。

translations.literal: He had a daughter Chunzhen, betrothed to the Duke of Qian's Mu clan; after the upheaval all word was cut off and she ended her days at home.
translations.idiomatic: He had a daughter named Chunzhen, betrothed to the Mu clan of the Duke of Qian; after the dynastic collapse all communication ceased, and she remained unmarried at home until her death.

sentences.zh: 純貞能詩，自署曰郭貞女。

translations.literal: Chunzhen could write poetry and signed herself the Maiden Guo the Chaste.
translations.idiomatic: Chunzhen could write poetry and signed herself the Chaste Maiden Guo.

sentences.zh: 都督所著有衡嶽集、止菴集、秋聲吟、西山片石集、破草奚集、補山堂集、些菴雜著等書。

translations.literal: Duxian's works include Hengyue Collection, Zhian Collection, Autumn Sounds, Western Mountain Stone Fragments, Pocao Xi Collection, Bushan Hall Collection, Xie'an Miscellany, and other books.
translations.idiomatic: Duxian authored the Hengyue Collection, Zhian Collection, Autumn Sounds, Western Mountain Stone Fragments, Pocao Xi Collection, Bushan Hall Collection, Xie'an Miscellany, and other works.

sentences.zh: 陶汝鼐，字仲調，一字密菴，寧鄉人。

translations.literal: Tao Runai, style name Zhongdiao, also styled Mihuan, a native of Ningxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Runai, courtesy name Zhongdiao, also known as Mihuan, was a native of Ningxiang.

sentences.zh: 與都賢交最篤。

translations.literal: His friendship with Duxian was deepest.
translations.idiomatic: His friendship with Guo Duxian was especially close.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，充拔貢生。

translations.literal: Early in Chongzhen he was selected as a tribute student.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Chongzhen reign he was selected as a tribute student.

sentences.zh: 會帝幸太學，群臣請復高皇積分法，祭酒顧錫疇奏薦汝鼐才，特賜第一，詔題名勒石太學。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Imperial Academy, ministers asked to restore the founding emperor's point system; the libationer Gu Xidie memorialized Runai's talent; he was specially granted first place and an edict ordered his name carved in stone at the Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Imperial Academy, the ministers asked to restore the founding emperor's point system; Libationer Gu Xidie memorialized Runai's talent, and he was specially awarded first place, with an edict ordering his name carved in stone at the Academy.

sentences.zh: 除五品官，不拜，乞留監肄業。

translations.literal: He was appointed a fifth-rank official but did not accept, begging to remain and study at the Directorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to a fifth-rank post but declined to take office, asking instead to remain at the Directorate and continue his studies.

sentences.zh: 癸酉舉於鄉，兩中會試副榜。

translations.literal: In the guiyou year he passed the provincial examination and twice placed on the metropolitan examination's supplementary list.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiyou year he passed the provincial examination and twice placed on the supplementary list of the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 南渡後，薙發溈山，號忍頭陀。

translations.literal: After the southward crossing he shaved his head on Mount Wei and styled himself Monk Ren.
translations.idiomatic: After the southward crossing he tonsured on Mount Wei and took the name Monk Ren.

sentences.zh: 生平內行篤，父歾，哀慕終身。

translations.literal: Throughout life his inner conduct was earnest; when his father died he mourned to the end of his days.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life his private conduct was earnest; when his father died he mourned him to the end of his days.

sentences.zh: 事母曲盡孝養，處族黨多厚德，嘗為人雪奇冤，冒險難，活千餘人，然不自言也。

translations.literal: Serving his mother he fulfilled filial nurture in every way; among kin he showed much generous virtue; he once cleared a singular injustice for others, braved danger, and saved more than a thousand lives, yet never spoke of it himself.
translations.idiomatic: In serving his mother he was thoroughly filial; among his clan he showed great generosity; he once righted a grave injustice for others, braved danger, and saved more than a thousand lives, yet never spoke of it himself.

sentences.zh: 詩古文有奇氣，著有廣西涯樂府、古集、寄雲樓集、褐玉堂集、嘉樹堂集，都賢為序而行之。

translations.literal: His poetry and ancient prose had singular force; his works include Guangxi Cliff Ballads, Ancient Collection, Cloud-Sending Tower Collection, Brown Jade Hall Collection, and Jia Tree Hall Collection—Duxian wrote prefaces and published them.
translations.idiomatic: His poetry and prose had a singular force; he wrote the Guangxi Cliff Ballads, Ancient Collection, Cloud-Sending Tower Collection, Brown Jade Hall Collection, and Jia Tree Hall Collection, which Duxian prefaced and published.

sentences.zh: 有「生同里、長同學、出處患難同時同志」之語。

translations.literal: There is the saying: "Born in the same village, grew studying together, in going forth and in hardship at the same time with the same will."
translations.idiomatic: Of their bond there is the saying: "Born in the same village, raised in the same studies, alike in going forth and in hardship, alike in purpose and in will."

sentences.zh: 李世熊，字元仲，寧化人。

translations.literal: Li Shixiong, style name Yuanzhong, a native of Ninghua.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shixiong, courtesy name Yuanzhong, was a native of Ninghua.

sentences.zh: 明諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate of the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a licentiate under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 少負奇氣，植大節，更危險，死生弗渝。

translations.literal: In youth he bore singular spirit, planted great integrity, faced changing peril, and life and death did not alter him.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he possessed a singular spirit, upheld great integrity, faced shifting dangers, and would not waver in life or death.

sentences.zh: 篤交遊，敢任難事。

translations.literal: Devoted in friendship, he dared undertake difficult affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted in friendship, he dared take on difficult affairs.

sentences.zh: 生平喜讀異書，博聞強記。

translations.literal: Throughout life he delighted in reading unusual books and had broad hearing and strong memory.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout his life he delighted in reading unusual books and possessed a broad memory.

sentences.zh: 年八十，讀書恆至夜分始休。

translations.literal: At eighty he still read constantly until the night watch before resting.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty he still read constantly, often not resting until the night watch.

sentences.zh: 六經、諸子百家靡不貫究，然獨好韓非、屈原、韓愈之書。

translations.literal: The Six Classics and the hundred schools he mastered without exception, yet he especially loved the books of Han Fei, Qu Yuan, and Han Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the Six Classics and the hundred schools without exception, yet especially loved the writings of Han Fei, Qu Yuan, and Han Yu.

sentences.zh: 其為文，沉深峭刻，奧博離奇，悲憤之音，稱其所遇。

translations.literal: His writing was deep, stern, and incisive, abstruse and vast and strange; notes of grief and indignation matched what he encountered.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was deep, stern, and incisive, abstruse, vast, and strange, with notes of grief and indignation that matched what he had endured.

sentences.zh: 縱

translations.literal: Freely
translations.idiomatic: When he held forth

sentences.zh: 論古今興亡，儒生出處，及江南北利害，備兵屯田水利諸大政，輒慷慨欷歔，涔涔泣下不止。

translations.literal: discoursing on the rise and fall of past and present, the going forth of Confucian scholars, and the advantages and harms of north and south of the Yangtze, and on great policies such as troops, garrison farming, and water conservancy, he would sigh with emotion and weep without cease.
translations.idiomatic: on the rise and fall of past and present, the choices of Confucian scholars in office and withdrawal, and the advantages and harms north and south of the Yangtze, as well as great policies of troops, garrison farming, and water conservancy, he would sigh with emotion and weep without cease.

sentences.zh: 年十六，補弟子員，旋中天啟元年副榜，以興化司李佘昌祚得其文，爭元於主司弗得，袖其卷去，曰：「須後作元也。

translations.literal: At sixteen he became a student member; soon after he placed on the supplementary list of the first year of Tianqi; the Xinghua magistrate She Changzuo obtained his essay and contended for top place with the chief examiner but could not win, and took his scroll away, saying: "He must later be made top."
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he became a student member; soon after he placed on the supplementary list in the first year of Tianqi. She Changzuo, magistrate of Xinghua, obtained his examination essay and argued with the chief examiner that it should rank first, but could not prevail; he took the scroll away, saying, "He must be made top place later."

sentences.zh: 」典閩試者，爭欲物色之為重。

translations.literal: " Those administering the Fujian examination all contended to seek him out as a weight.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who ran the Fujian examinations all sought him out as a prize candidate.

sentences.zh: 甲申後，自號寒支道人，屏居不見客。

translations.literal: After jiashen he styled himself the Han Branch Daoist, secluded himself, and did not receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: After the jiashen year he styled himself the Han Branch Daoist, lived in seclusion, and would not receive visitors.

sentences.zh: 徵書累下，固謝卻之。

translations.literal: Summonses came repeatedly and he firmly declined them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial summonses came repeatedly, and he firmly declined them all.

sentences.zh: 凡守、令、監司、鎮將至其門者，罕能一識面。

translations.literal: Of prefects, magistrates, surveillance commissioners, and military commanders who came to his door, few could meet his face once.
translations.idiomatic: Of prefects, magistrates, surveillance commissioners, and military commanders who came to his door, few ever met his face even once.

sentences.zh: 閩中擁唐王監國，用大學士黃道周、禮部侍郎曹學佺、都察院何楷薦，徵拜翰林博士，辭不赴。

translations.literal: When Fujian supported the Prince of Tang as regent, Huang Daozhou as Grand Secretary, Cao Xueqian as Vice Minister of Rites, and He Kai of the Censorate recommended him, he was summoned as Hanlin Academician Doctor but declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Fujian supported the Prince of Tang as regent, Huang Daozhou as grand secretary, Cao Xueqian as vice minister of rites, and He Kai of the censorate recommended him, he was summoned as Hanlin Academician Doctor but declined to go.

sentences.zh: 嘗上書道周，感憤時事。

translations.literal: He once sent a letter to Daozhou, moved and indignant at the affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote to Huang Daozhou, moved and indignant at the affairs of the day.

sentences.zh: 及道周殉節，走福州請褒卹，時卹問其孤嫠。

translations.literal: When Daozhou died a martyr's death, he hurried to Fuzhou to request posthumous honors; at the time the condolence inquiry asked about his widows and orphans.
translations.idiomatic: When Daozhou died for the dynasty, he rushed to Fuzhou to seek posthumous honors, and the court's inquiry extended to the widows and orphans he had left behind.

sentences.zh: 順治初，師入閩，有齮齕於郡帥者，帥遣某生移書，逼入都，且言：「不出山，禍不測。

translations.literal: In early Shunzhi, when the army entered Fujian, someone bore a grudge against him with the prefectural commander; the commander sent a certain student with a letter, pressing him to enter the capital, and saying, "If you do not come forth from the mountains, disaster is unforeseeable."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, after the Qing army entered Fujian, an enemy at court persuaded the prefectural commander to send a student with a letter demanding that he come to the capital. "If you refuse to leave the hills," it warned, "you cannot tell what calamity may follow."

sentences.zh: 」世熊復之曰：「死生有命，豈遂懸於要津之手？

translations.literal: Shixiong replied: "Life and death have their allotted span—how could they hang on the hands of men at the crossroads?"
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong wrote back: "Life and death are fated. How could they depend on the whim of men who hold the gates of power?"

sentences.zh: 且某年四十八矣，諸葛瘁躬之日，僅少一年；

translations.literal: Moreover, I am already forty-eight; the day Zhuge Liang wore himself out in service was only one year less;
translations.idiomatic: Besides, I am forty-eight already—only one year short of the age at which Zhuge Liang wore himself out in service;

sentences.zh: 文山盡節之辰，已多一歲。

translations.literal: the day Wenshan exhausted his integrity was already one year more.
translations.idiomatic: and a full year older than Wen Tianxiang when he gave his life for the Song.

sentences.zh: 何能抑情違性，重取羞辱哉！

translations.literal: How could I suppress feeling and violate my nature, and again invite disgrace!
translations.idiomatic: How could I stifle my nature and invite shame a second time!"

sentences.zh: 」時蜚語騰沸，世熊矢死不為動，疑謗旋亦釋。

translations.literal: At the time slander boiled up; Shixiong vowed to die and would not be moved; suspicion and calumny soon also dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Slander swirled around him, but Shixiong swore he would rather die than yield, and before long the suspicion lifted.

sentences.zh: 世熊既以文章氣節著一時，名大震。

translations.literal: Shixiong, having become famous in his time for literary works and moral integrity, his name greatly shook the age.
translations.idiomatic: By then Shixiong was renowned for his writing and his integrity, and his fame resounded far and wide.

sentences.zh: 辛卯、壬辰間，建昌潰賊黃希孕剽掠過寧化，有卒摘其園中二橘，希孕立鞭之，駐馬園側，視卒盡過乃行。

translations.literal: Between xinmao and renchen, the routed bandit Huang Xiyun of Jianchang plundered past Ninghua; a soldier picked two oranges from his garden; Xiyun at once had him flogged, halted his horse beside the garden, and watched until all the soldiers had passed before moving on.
translations.idiomatic: Between the xinmao and renchen years the routed rebel Huang Xiyun of Jianchang raided past Ninghua. When a soldier picked two oranges from Shixiong's garden, Xiyun had him flogged on the spot, then waited on horseback until every man had passed before he rode on.

sentences.zh: 粵寇至，燔民屋，火及其園，賊魁劉大勝遣卒撲救之，曰：「奈何壞李公居？

translations.literal: When Guangdong bandits came, they burned people's houses; the fire reached his garden; the bandit chief Liu Dasheng sent soldiers to beat it out, saying, "How can we destroy Master Li's dwelling?"
translations.idiomatic: When Guangdong rebels came they burned the people's houses, and the flames reached his garden. The rebel leader Liu Dasheng sent men to put the fire out, crying, "How can we destroy Master Li's home?"

sentences.zh: 」當時雖匹夫匹婦，無不知有寒支子者。

translations.literal: At the time even every common man and woman knew there was one called Hanzhizi.
