translations.idiomatic: In those days even the humblest man or woman knew the name Hanzhizi.

sentences.zh: 世熊積壘塊胸中，每放浪山水，以寫其牢騷不平之概。

translations.literal: Shixiong piled grievances in his breast; he often wandered freely among mountains and waters to set down the mood of his imprisoned resentment and injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Grievance piled up in Shixiong's heart. He often wandered the mountains and rivers to pour out the anger and sorrow he could not otherwise release.

sentences.zh: 嘗詣西江，交魏禧、魏禮、彭士望諸子，相與泛彭蠡，登廬山絕頂。

translations.literal: Once he went to the West River region, befriended Wei Xi, Wei Li, Peng Shiwang, and others, and together they sailed on Poyang Lake and climbed to the summit of Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He once traveled to the West River country, where he befriended Wei Xi, Wei Li, Peng Shiwang, and others. Together they boated on Poyang Lake and climbed to the top of Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 追維闖賊橫行時事，痛悼如絕，淚下如泉湧，不能禁也。

translations.literal: Recalling how the roving bandits of the rebel regime had run rampant, he grieved as if his breath were cut off; tears poured like a spring and he could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: As he recalled the days when the rebel armies ran riot, grief overwhelmed him. Tears gushed forth like a spring and he could not hold them back.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠反，遣偽使敦聘，世熊嚴拒之。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, he sent false envoys with earnest invitations; Shixiong sternly refused them.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rose in rebellion he sent envoys with repeated invitations, but Shixiong refused them outright.

sentences.zh: 自春徂冬，堅臥不起，乃得免。

translations.literal: From spring to winter he lay firm in bed and would not rise, and so escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: From spring through winter he kept to his bed and would not rise, and so escaped being drawn in.

sentences.zh: 世熊山居四十餘年，鄉人宗之，爭趨決事。

translations.literal: Shixiong dwelt in the mountains more than forty years; the people of his district looked up to him and all rushed to him to settle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong lived in the mountains for more than forty years. The people of his district revered him and flocked to him to settle their disputes.

sentences.zh: 有為不善者，曰：「不使李公知也。

translations.literal: When someone did wrong, he would say, "Don't let Master Li know."
translations.idiomatic: If someone did wrong, people would say, "Don't let Master Li find out."

sentences.zh: 」晚自號媿菴，顏其齋曰「但月」。

translations.literal: In his later years he styled himself Hermitage of Shame and inscribed his study "Only the Moon."
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he called himself the Hermitage of Shame and named his study Only the Moon.

sentences.zh: 所著有寒支集、寧化縣志、本行錄、經正錄、狗馬史記等。

translations.literal: His writings include the Hanzhi Collection, the Gazetteer of Ninghua County, the Record of Original Conduct, the Record of Rectifying the Classics, the Dog-and-Horse Historical Notes, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His works include the Hanzhi Collection, the Gazetteer of Ninghua County, the Record of Original Conduct, the Record of Rectifying the Classics, the Dog-and-Horse Historical Notes, and others.

sentences.zh: 年八十五，卒於家。

translations.literal: At the age of eighty-five he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 世熊有三弟，早世，遺子女，撫育裝遣之。

translations.literal: Shixiong had three younger brothers who died young, leaving sons and daughters; he reared them and provided dowries and send-offs.
translations.idiomatic: He had three younger brothers who died young and left children behind. He raised those children and saw to their marriages and departures.

sentences.zh: 饋遺其親戚終身。

translations.literal: He sent gifts to his kinsmen throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: He supported his kinsmen with gifts all his life.

sentences.zh: 又獨建祖祠，修祖墓，編述九世以來宗譜。

translations.literal: He also alone built an ancestral hall, repaired the ancestral tombs, and compiled the clan genealogy from nine generations back.
translations.idiomatic: He built the ancestral hall himself, restored the family graves, and compiled the clan genealogy back nine generations.

sentences.zh: 凡祭祀，必親必謹。

translations.literal: In all sacrifices he was personally present and scrupulous.
translations.idiomatic: For every sacrifice he was present in person and meticulous in observance.

sentences.zh: 父母忌日，則減餐絕宴會。

translations.literal: On his parents' death anniversaries he reduced his meals and cut off banquets.
translations.idiomatic: On his parents' death anniversaries he ate sparingly and held no feasts.

sentences.zh: 元旦，展先人遺像，則泣下沾襟，拜伏不能起，蓋其孝友出於天性雲。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day, when he unrolled the portraits of his forebears, tears soaked his robe and he bowed prostrate unable to rise—such was the filial affection that sprang from his inborn nature.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day, when he unrolled his ancestors' portraits, tears soaked his robe and he bowed until he could not rise. His filial devotion sprang from inborn nature.

sentences.zh: 談遷，字孺木，原名以訓，海寧人。

translations.literal: Tan Qian, courtesy name Rumu, original name Yixun, was a native of Haining.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Qian, styled Rumu, born Yixun, came from Haining.

sentences.zh: 初為諸生。

translations.literal: At first he was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a licentiate scholar.

sentences.zh: 南都立，以中書薦，召入史館，皆辭，曰：「餘豈以國家之不幸博一官耶？

translations.literal: When the Southern Capital was established, he was recommended as Secretariat Drafter and summoned to the Historiography Institute; he declined all, saying, "Would I trade on the state's misfortune to win an office?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Southern Capital was established he was recommended for the Secretariat and summoned to the Historiography Institute, but he refused everything. "Would I trade on the nation's misfortune for an office?" he said.

sentences.zh: 」未幾，歸里。

translations.literal: Before long he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went home.

sentences.zh: 遷肆力經史百家言，尤注心於明朝典故。

translations.literal: Qian devoted his strength to the classics, histories, and the hundred schools, especially fixing his mind on Ming-dynasty institutions and precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Qian threw himself into the classics, histories, and all schools of learning, with special attention to the institutions and precedents of the Ming.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂：「史之所憑者，實錄耳。

translations.literal: He once said: "What history relies on is the Veritable Records alone."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "History depends on nothing but the Veritable Records."

sentences.zh: 實錄見其表，其在裡者，已不可見。

translations.literal: The Veritable Records show the surface; what lies within is already invisible.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records show only the surface. What lies within them can no longer be seen.

sentences.zh: 況革除之事，楊文貞未免失實；

translations.literal: Moreover, in the matter of the Jianwen purge, Yang Wenzhong inevitably fell short of truth;
translations.idiomatic: As for the purge of the Jianwen reign, even Yang Wenzhong's account could not avoid distortion;

sentences.zh: 泰陵之盛，焦泌陽又多醜正；

translations.literal: in the splendor of the Tailing reign, Jiao Biyang moreover vilified the upright;
translations.idiomatic: under the glory of the Hongzhi reign, Jiao Biyang slandered the righteous;

sentences.zh: 神、熹之載筆者，皆逆奄之舍人。

translations.literal: those who wielded the brush under the Shenzong and Xizong reigns were all retainers of the eunuch faction.
translations.idiomatic: and the scribes of the Wanli and Tianqi reigns were all clients of the eunuch faction.

sentences.zh: 至於思陵十七年之憂勤惕厲，而太史遯荒，皇宬烈焰，國滅而史亦隨滅，普天心痛，莫甚於此！

translations.literal: As for the seventeen years of anxious diligence and vigilance under Sizong, yet the Grand Historian fled to the wilds, the imperial archives blazed, the state perished and history perished with it—under heaven no grief surpasses this!
translations.idiomatic: Worst of all were the seventeen years of anxious toil under the Chongzhen emperor, when the court historian fled into exile, the imperial archives burned, and the state and its history perished together. Under heaven no grief was greater!

sentences.zh: 」乃汰十五朝實錄，正其是非。

translations.literal: He therefore sifted the Veritable Records of fifteen reigns and corrected right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He sifted the Veritable Records of fifteen reigns and set right and wrong in order.

sentences.zh: 訪崇禎十七年邸報，補其缺文，成書，名曰國榷。

translations.literal: He sought the court gazettes of the seventeenth year of Chongzhen, supplemented their missing text, completed a book, and named it Guoque.
translations.idiomatic: He hunted down the court gazettes of Chongzhen's seventeenth year, filled in what was missing, and completed a book called Guoque.

sentences.zh: 當是時，人士身經喪亂，多欲追敘緣因，以顯來世，而見聞窄狹，無所憑藉。

translations.literal: At that time scholars who had lived through the calamity mostly wished to trace causes and narrate them to show posterity, yet their experience was narrow and they had nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Men who had lived through the collapse wanted to trace how it had happened and leave a record for posterity, but their own experience was narrow and they had nothing solid to build on.

sentences.zh: 聞遷有是書，思欲竊之為己有。

translations.literal: Hearing that Qian had this book, they thought to steal it and make it their own.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard that Qian had such a book, they wanted to seize it for themselves.

sentences.zh: 遷家貧，不見可欲者，夜有盜入其室，盡發藏橐以去。

translations.literal: Qian's family was poor and nothing desirable could be seen; by night a thief entered his room and emptied every stored chest and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was poor and kept nothing tempting in sight, yet one night a thief broke in and carried off everything he had stored away.

sentences.zh: 遷喟然曰：「吾手尚在，寧遂已乎？

translations.literal: Qian sighed and said, "My hands are still here—could I simply stop?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian sighed and said, "My hands are still mine. Am I to give up now?"

sentences.zh: 」從嘉善錢氏借書復成之。

translations.literal: He borrowed books from the Qian family of Jiashan and completed it again.
translations.idiomatic: He borrowed books from the Qian family of Jiashan and wrote the work again.

sentences.zh: 陽城張慎言目為奇士，折節下之。

translations.literal: Zhang Shenyan of Yangcheng regarded him as a rare man and lowered himself to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shenyan of Yangcheng saw him as a man of rare gifts and humbled himself to honor him.

sentences.zh: 慎言卒，遷方北走昌平，哭思陵，复欲赴陽城哭慎言，未至而卒，順治十二年冬十一月也。

translations.literal: When Shenyan died, Qian had just gone north to Changping and wept at Sizong's tomb; he again wished to go to Yangcheng to weep for Shenyan, but before arriving he died—it was the eleventh month of winter in the twelfth year of Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenyan died, Qian had just gone north to Changping to weep at the Chongzhen emperor's tomb. He set out for Yangcheng to mourn Shenyan but died on the way, in the eleventh month of winter in the twelfth year of Shunzhi.

sentences.zh: 黃宗羲為表其墓。

translations.literal: Huang Zongxi composed an epitaph for his tomb.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zongxi wrote the epitaph for his grave.

sentences.zh: 明末遺逸，守志不屈，身雖隱而心不死，至事不可為，發憤著書，欲託空文以見志，如遷者，其憂憤豈有已耶？

translations.literal: Remnant subjects of the late Ming who kept their integrity unbent—though the body hid, the heart did not die; when affairs could no longer be done, they vented anger in writing books, wishing to entrust empty words to show their will: for one like Qian, could his grief and indignation ever end?
translations.idiomatic: The loyalist survivors of the late Ming held to their principles though their bodies lived in hiding and their hearts never surrendered. When nothing more could be done, they poured their rage into books, trusting empty words to bear witness to their will. For a man like Qian, could grief and anger ever have an end?

sentences.zh: 故以附於各省遺逸之末。

translations.literal: Therefore he is appended at the end of the remnant subjects of the various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: That is why he is placed at the close of the loyalist biographies from the provinces.
